articleTitle: Weapon Object Detection Using Quantized YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Video surveillance is essential for creating a secure and hassle-free environment in all areas of life. It helps identify theft, detect unusual events in crowded locations, and monitor the suspicious behavior of individuals. However, monitoring surveillance cameras manually is quite challenging, and thus, fully automated surveillance with smart video-capturing capabilities is gaining popularity. This approach uses deep learning methodology to remotely monitor unusual actions with accurate information about the location, time of occurrence, and identification of criminals. Detecting criminal conduct in public settings is difficult due to the complexity of real-world scenarios. CCTV cameras can record suspicious incidents in public areas, such as carrying weapons, which helps authorities to take preventive measures to protect citizens. The proposed system employs the state-of-the-art YOLOv8 model for real-time weapon detection, which is faster, more accurate, and better than YOLOv5. To ensure fast performance, the weights of YOLOv8 were quantized. In our experiments, we evaluated the performance of the YOLOv8 and YOLOv5 models for weapon detection. The mean Average Precision (mAP) value achieved using YOLOv8 was 90.1%, which outperformed the mAP value of 89.1% obtained with YOLOv5. Furthermore, by applying weight quantization to the YOLOv8 model, we reduced the inference time by 15% compared to the original YOLOv8 configuration.

articleTitle: Optimizing RIS-assisted Wireless Communication Systems with Non-Linear Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) or Intelli-gent reflecting surfaces (IRS) are synonyms to a highly disruptive technology being proposed for beyond 5G (B5G)/6G Wireless Communications due to its environment controllable, power saving and spectral efficient features. Internet-of- Things (loT) devices demand for longer battery life with considerable data rate. To address this concern, simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) is currently being explored in combination with RIS. In this paper, we consider a time-switching (TS) SWIPT architecture with non-linear energy harvesting (EH) at the loT node. The concerned base station provides information and energy concurrently to the loT node through RIS. We formulate EH maximization problem under various sets of constraints, which can be solved using the proposed iterative optimization algorithm following a divide-and-conquer methodology. Numerical evaluation confers that it is necessary to have a larger number of RIS elements to get maximum benefit in terms of EH.

Author Keywords: Si- multaneous wireless power and information transfer (SWIPT)

articleTitle: GMPP Improvement with Fewer Power Peaks and Lower Mismatch Losses Using a New Hybrid BIPV Array Configuration
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Maximum power production and efficiency of large building integrated photovoltaic (BIPV) or solar photovoltaic (PV) array installations are greatly reduced by partial shadowing (PS), which is a considerable barrier. This paper's major goal is to conduct a thorough examination of the existing hybrid PV array configurations with the proposed hybrid BIPV array configuration under four diverse scenarios of PS using the MATLAB-Simulink software. Series-Parallel Total-Cross-Tied (SP-TCT), Bridge-Linked TCT (BL-TCT), Honey-Combed TCT (HC-TCT), and BL-HC are the existing hybrid arrays utilized for analysis. Sandwich Bridge-Linked Total-Cross-Tied (S-BL-TCT) hybrid BIPV array is the new configuration proposed in this research. Five different existing and proposed hybrid <tex>$8 \times 6$</tex> PV and BIPV array configurations are assessed for their performance in terms of the global maximum power point (GMPP), voltage and current at the GMPP, open-circuit voltage (OCV), short-circuit current (SCC), the number of power peaks (PPs), shading loss (SL), mismatch loss (ML), fill factor (FF), and efficiency <tex>$(\eta)$</tex>. According to the performance evaluation, the proposed S-BL-TCT configuration increases GMPP by 5.63 %, lowers ML by 4.2 %, and enhances FF & <tex>$\eta$</tex> by 2.33 % and 0.43 %, respectively. In severe instances of PS, the proposed S-BL-TCT array reduces the number of PPs created.

articleTitle: Analysis of Wind Resource on a Site using Wind Turbine Mathematical Model on MATLAB SIMULINK
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: One of the important parameter in wind turbine installation is finding amount of energy the turbine would generate in a particular site. This paper focuses on the analysis of wind resources on a particular site using a wind turbine mathematical model on MATLAB SIMULINK. The study aims to determine the potential wind power generation capacity of the site by simulating various wind scenarios and analysing the wind turbine mathematical model. The analysis involves the use of various parameters such as wind speed, radius of wind turbine blade, air density, and rotational speed of shaft, pitch angle, performance coefficient and ratio of tip speed to assess the performance of the turbine. The results of the study show that the turbine mathematical model on MATLAB SIMULINK is an effective tool for analysing wind resources and determining the potential wind power generation capacity of a particular site. The findings of this study can be useful for decision-makers in the renewable energy sector to make informed decisions on wind power projects.

articleTitle: Mitigation of Power Quality Issues during Electric Vehicle Integration
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Transportation system is considered as the second largest source of carbon emissions after power generation. EVs (Electric Vehicles) play major role in reducing carbon emissions. Integration of EVs into the grid not only reduces carbon emissions but also protects environment. However there exists, many challenges during this integration. The major challenges faced during integration are overloading of power grid, power quality (PQ) issues, supply demand imbalance, increased peak demand, frequency deviation, energy losses, reduced stability and reliability, battery degradation and high investment cost. In this regard, few concerned issues from the above are considered and they are being mitigated by using RES as the main power supply. When these sources are unable to provide sufficient power to charge the vehicles, we rely on the energy stored in BESS for vehicle charging. In this event that BESS is also incapable of meeting the power demand, the Grid serves as an alternative power source for vehicle charging. This mitigation technique is being discussed and demonstrated using the MATLAB Simulink platform.

articleTitle: Dynamical behaviour in a peak ripple based V2 controlled buck converter
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: In this paper the dynamical behaviour has been explored in V<sup>2</sup> controlled buck converter. This V<sup>2</sup> modulation method basically falls under ripple based control methods as output ripple voltage is used to control the converter. Mathematical model has been derived using state space equations. The bifurcation phenomena have been studied. The dependency of the system behavior on the variation of its parameters has been explored and the parameter space diagrams have been obtained. Dependency of the converter operation on effective series resistance (ESR) of the output capacitor has also been explained. This study is immensely helpful for the design and operation of converter.

articleTitle: A Survey on Weather Prediction using Big Data and Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: From the different studies of recent papers using Google Scholar, the study examined in 2018 the most relevant scientific articles published which are 500 that dealt with the field of numerical weather prediction and climate with machine learning methods. In the abstracts, the most common subjects of interest were accepted, and in between them, a few were investigated further: wind energy and photovoltaic, physics of atmospheric and development of numerical weather prediction; parameterizations, severe occurrences, and change of climate in climate research. The precipitation, pressure, radiation, temperature, and wind, like meteorological fields, Random Forests, Artificial Neural Networks, Deep Learning, XGBoost-like methods, and Support Vector Machine were discussed. Further, Australia, India, China, United States, and Germany like countries were there to extract data using the created database on these topics. To predict the future research by authors in the direction of these domains by conducting critical evaluations of the literature, machine learning with a major conclusion being approached will be a prominent element in future forecasting of the weather. This study also offers a way for doing a systematic review of the literature for big data analytical techniques in the forecasting of weather.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Logic Control Based Energy Management in Hybrid Microgrid System
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Hybrid microgrids are attractive design that can be used for a variety of purposes, especially in stand-alone power generation systems like lighting, water pumping, etc. Energy management control will be required due to the variety of energy sources. The oversight of a hybrid Wind/Photovoltaic system with battery storage is discussed in this study. The proposed system's power balancing is based on an intelligent supervisor that uses fuzzy logic control. It enables the determination of the various operating processes of the hybrid energy system based on weather conditions. The research was conducted using Matlab/Simulink. The presented results demonstrate the viability of the proposed control system.

articleTitle: Experimental Investigation of Voltage Regulation Using ELC for Two Self-Excited Induction Generators Connected in Parallel
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Self-excited induction generator (SEIG) is one of the promising sources of power generation in the off-grid mode of the micro hydro-power system. To have a more reliable source in rural, parallel operation of sources is much needed, but paralleling two SEIG with different ratings is always a challenge. The requirement of loads can be full fill by connecting two sources in parallel but in the off-grid system, be it parallel or single source, the terminal voltage is not constant and vary with loads. An attempt is made to operate two SEIGs with different ratings in parallel and keep the terminal voltage constant using an electronic load controller. The proposed method is tested using MATLAB and validated with hardware experiments.

articleTitle: Reduced Switch Components Multilevel Inverter
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: The multilevel inverter is proposed with reduced switches count. The basic topology require ten switches to generate five level in output voltage as levels increases number of switches decreases compared to cascaded H-bridge structure. Proposed topology can be operated in symmetrical and asymmetrical configurations. Additive operation of DC sources generates output in the symmetrical configuration, additive and subtractive operation of DC sources generate output in asymmetrical configuration of proposed topology. Sinusoidal Pulse Width Modulation(SPWM) techniques is used to generate switching signals to inverter. Effectiveness of proposed topology is verified by MATLAB/SIMULINK software.

articleTitle: Analysis of Defuzzification Methods of a Fuzzy Logic Controller for Priority Control of Electric Vehicle Charging
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: In today's world the pollution level is very high due to the massive number of vehicles based on conventional fuels; this creates a need of shifting the transportation sector on electric vehicles as much as possible. This increasing demand of EV requires better charging facilities which can be only achieved when there is a proper balance between the user demand and the power supply in the grid at the correct locations. To achieve this balance in the grid, energy savings and efficiency of energy generation and distribution all the charging stations must be properly utilized by the EV users and for this a fuzzy logic controller is proposed through this work which provides proper interdependency between the user's EV and the power system grid on the basis of the parameters provided to the controller from both ends. The proposed fuzzy logic controller takes state of charge of vehicle, distance between the EV and the charging station and variation in charging cost as the inputs, and keeping the charging time, charging level and other parameters in the check, provides the necessity of EV user to head towards a particular charging station as the output which enables the user to smartly choose the most suitable charging station, present n different routes, during periods and modalities that highly favors the smart grid operation, energy savings and economic efficiency. This work also analyses various methods to achieve the same task and concludes the best method to attain the same balance in the system as result with a better accuracy which adheres the benefit of both the EV user and the smart grid.

articleTitle: Dynamic Analysis of Vector Controlled PMSM with Constant Torque Angle Control Strategy Using Artificial Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: This paper proposes an AI approach to enhance the PMSM drive systems through an ANN based speed controller. Due to its great efficiency and precise control capabilities, PMSM drives are broadly used in industrial applications. However, achieving optimal speed control remains a challenging task, especially under varying operating conditions and disturbances. To address this, the proposed ANN-based speed controller utilizes to approximate the complex nonlinear relationship between motor torque and control input. Through adaptive learning, the controller effectively adapts to changing system dynamics, uncertainties, and disturbances, resulting in improved speed tracking accuracy, disturbance rejection, and robustness. Simulation results shows the better performance of the ANN controller compared to conventional techniques, making it a promising solution for enhancing PMSM drive system performance in various industrial applications.

articleTitle: Maximizing Coverage Efficiency in Wireless Networks using GWO: An Investigation of Hexagonal and Circular Tiling for Edge Server Placement
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Edge servers (ESs) are crucial for enhancing performance and reliability in modern network systems. They minimize network latency, improve responsiveness, and optimize network utilization by bringing computational resources closer to end-users. This work explores the necessity of edge servers in modern network systems and their contribution to providing efficient and reliable quality of service (QoS). However, the conventional circle shape of edge server coverage is impractical due to its inherent drawbacks. The hexagonal range has emerged as a better alternative due to its balanced and uniform distribution of coverage areas. The Edge Server Placement Problem (ESPP) is NP-hard owing to multiple Base Stations (BS) and Edge Servers (ESs). Stochastic evolutionary metaheuristics are a natural choice. This study provides a comprehensive analysis of various approaches for edge server coverage, including the Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO), Top-First approach, Random approach, and K-mean approach, among others. The open-source Shanghai Telecom dataset is used to evaluate the efficacy of these approaches with respect to QoS metrics such as work-load balance, energy consumption, and server utilisation rate. Our findings demonstrate that the GWO approach outperforms compared to other conventional approach K-mean by 8.60% in workload distribution, 5.19% in utilization rate and reduces energy consumption by 31.60%.

articleTitle: Geothermal Energy-Future Energy Opportunity for India
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: As a developing nation, India has always been committed to looking for more alternative energy sources for sustainable development. By 2030, India's total capacity for power production would be about 820GW out of that, over 500GW will be fossil-free energy. India has a great deal of potential to lead the way in producing geothermal energy that is both environmentally friendly and economically viable. As per current data, geothermal energy would contribute to the production of 8.3% of the world's electricity. In India, geothermal energy is in the earliest stages of development. However, around 340 hot springs have been found by the Indian Geological Survey. The geothermal provinces of India have the potential to generate around 10,600 MW of electricity, which is equivalent to the entire world's geothermal capacity. India will play a bigger role in this sector in the next few years because of strong international collaboration with nations including the United States, Philippines, Mexico, and New Zealand.

articleTitle: Non-Linear Kalman Filter Based SOC Estimation of a Lithium-Ion Battery Pack Considering Cell Balancing
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Precise estimation of state of charge while taking cell balancing technology into account is one of a battery management system's key advantages. For the battery pack to operate safely and to avoid being overcharged and undercharged, cell balance is crucial. Because of the intricate characteristics of the battery parameters with regard to SOC and temperature, it is very difficult to measure the SOC directly. The 1RC model has been used to depict the dynamic behavior of a single cell. To estimate the SOC using different model-based filtering procedures, a battery pack model in a 13s10p configuration has been developed and simulated over a drive cycle. Based on the measured voltage, current, temperature, and SOC, the battery pack is balanced.

articleTitle: Enhanced Power Factor Correction and Voltage Stability in Electric Spring Circuits Using Double Fuzzy Logic and Fuzzy PI Controllers
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Power factor and voltage stability in electrical networks have been significantly challenged as a result of the growth of nonlinear loads and renewable energy sources. In this research, an enhanced control approach for Electric Spring (ES) circuits is presented. The primary focuses of this control method are to improve power factor correction and preserve voltage stability under a variety of different operating circumstances. To improve the performance of the ES circuit control system in both undervoltage and overvoltage scenarios, a double fuzzy logic controller, as well as a fuzzy PI controller, have been included in the system. To determine whether or not the suggested control technique is successful, a MATLAB Simulink simulation is carried out. The results of the simulation show that the power factor has significantly improved, with values as high as 0.97 being achieved in overvoltage scenarios and as low as 0.99 being achieved in undervoltage settings. In addition, the findings demonstrate that the suggested control strategy is capable of preserving voltage and power stability, hence proving the potential of the double fuzzy logic controller as well as the fuzzy PI controller in applications that take place in the real world. The findings of this study provide important new perspectives on the design of sophisticated control solutions for power factor correction and voltage regulation in electrical systems.

articleTitle: Modelling and Control of Synthetic Inertia Controller for Modular Multilevel Converter Fed HVDC Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Increasing inertia of the grid connected system using HVDC converter integrated wind farm system is a popular solution now-a-days. This paper deals with such a system with appropriate modelling and control of synthetic inertia of the grid connected system. VSC-HVDC based Modular Multilevel Converter (MMC) and its internal controllers (DC Voltage and current controller) are employed for the application along with inertia emulation control and generator emulation control. Coordinated control technique is implemented in which wind turbines participate in the frequency support of the main grid along with stored energy in the MMC DC link without the use of communication cables. This paper emphasizes the effect of the design of various control loops in the synthetic inertia modelling and a detailed frequency domain modelling is carried out for different control loops to analyse the performance of the system. The concept is validated through PLECS based back-to-back MMC interfacing main grid and wind system through 400km HVDC line.

articleTitle: Class Topper Optimizer for Multi-Objective Cost Optimization in Smart Grid Using Demand Side Management Program
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Demand side management (DSM) is widely utilized in Smart Grid for its reliable features, flexibility, and cost benefits that it offers to customers in the reduction of the energy bill. In smart grid, all participants of the electricity market i.e., electricity users, demand response aggregator, and utility operator wish to improve individual economic benefits. It is quite challenging to simultaneously ensure financial advantage for all participants. In the current paper, a multi-objective problem is formulated considering all objectives of all the participants using the DSM program. The multi-objective DSM problem is optimized by a meta-heuristic optimization algorithm: Class Topper optimization (CTO). The goal is to schedule power production and load demand optimally for a given day in order to reduce peak loads, raise load factors, reduce operational costs of power generation, and simultaneously optimize advantages for all market participants in the electrical sector. The simulation's findings show that the ongoing methodology is capable of minimizing the cost of electricity generation and ensuring optimal benefit to all entities of the power market simultaneously. The outcomes are contrasted with other optimization strategy to demonstrate the viability of the current approach to deal with the IEEE 39-bus test framework.

articleTitle: Machine Learning based SoC Estimation for Li-Ion Battery
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Accurate State of Charge (SoC) estimation is critical for the efficient and safe operation of lithium-ion (Li-ion) batteries. Traditional methods for SoC estimation have limitations, and recent research has focused on using machine learning techniques to improve SoC estimation accuracy. In this research article, we present a study on SoC estimation for Li-ion batteries using machine learning techniques. We collected a dataset of battery voltage, current, and temperature measurements and used machine learning algorithms to estimate SoC. We compared the performance of machine learning algorithms with traditional methods such as coulomb counting and open-circuit voltage (OCV) method. Our results show that machine learning algorithms outperform traditional methods in estimating SoC, with an average error of less than 1 %. We discuss the advantages and limitations of using machine learning for SoC estimation and the potential for future research in this area. The findings of this study have implications for the development of battery management systems that can improve battery performance, safety, and lifetime.

articleTitle: On Underground Coal Mine Environment Monitoring with LoRa Range Extension
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: The present work proposes a wireless sensor network for underground coal mine environment monitoring using LoRa communication technology. The system consists of several inexpensive IoT sensors to assess environmental factors including temperature, humidity, air quality, and gas concentration. The designed monitoring unit is connected to the LoRaWAN network so that the units can interact with one another and also with the central server placed in the control room located above the ground. The work also presents a technique to extend the range of LoRa nodes so as to increase the coverage of LoRa network by relaying messages between devices and gateways inside the mine. Additionally a method based on spreading factor (SF) optimization is utilised for range extension. This work adjusts the SF of LoRa transmissions based on the distance between the devices. The range extension technique, which is integrated into the firmware of the devices, greatly extends the range and improves the dependability of LoRa communications in underground mines.

articleTitle: Hardware Acceleration of Pre-trained Networks for Colorectal Polyp Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: The objective of the research is to identify a pre-trained Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) with faster inference time for classification of colorectal polyps on a Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) device. Basically, Deep Learning(DL) models are trained and executed using Graphical Processing Units (GPUs) having high processing capacity, but those devices consume more power during execution. DL models that are appropriate for real-time miniature instruments must be implemented with low-power consumption. This paper evaluates the performance of relevant polyp classification models using FPGA (Avnet Ultra96-V2) and GPU (Quadro RTX 5000). The CNN models are trained on GPU and then deployed for inference on FPGA using the VITIS-AI platform and PYNQ framework. The MobileNetV2 performs classification with 88% accuracy and least inference time of 2.60 seconds at a throughput of 176 frames per second on FPGA. A precise comparison of the throughput and power consumption during execution on GPU and FPGA are provided. The FPGA device is found to perform <tex>$\mathbf{1}.\mathbf{25}\times$</tex> faster than GPU in terms of throughput while using <tex>$\mathbf{40}\times$</tex> less power with a negligible reduction in accuracy.

articleTitle: Solar Power Forecasting Using Hybrid Model
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: The significance of forecasting has been increasing in power systems due to the more usage of renewable energy sources. Renewable energy sources such as solar energy, which is very intermittent in nature. Hence, to capture this nature, Deep learning (DL) based techniques are required. Because DL-based techniques learn quickly from patterns and deal with intermittent changes in load and renewable sources. This study proposes DL technique-based convolution neural network (CNN) - long short-term memory (LSTM) hybrid model to forecast solar energy. This allows the LSTM to learn features from the input data that have been learned by CNN. Further, 15 minutes of solar power generation data for one year from Visvesvaraya National Institute of Technology (VNIT), Nagpur is used as the benchmark data to evaluate the hybrid model. This study considers a novel meteorological factor and compares that with without considering a meteorological factor. Moreover, CNN and LSTM individual DL models were developed, analyzed, and tested for the same VNIT data for forecasting the 15-minute solar power generation. The proposed hybrid model is compared with individual LSTM and CNN models in terms of performance evaluation matrices i.e., The root mean squared error (RMSE), the mean squared error (MSE), the mean absolute error (MAE), the mean absolute percentage error (MAPE), and the coefficient of determination (R-Squared) are all measures of error. The percentage improvement from the individual model and the proposed hybrid model has been evaluated with and without considering meteorological factors. The proposed model improves the efficiency by 0.45% and 21.31%, as compared to LSTM and CNN by considering metrological factors respectively. Similarly, it improves without considering metrological factors 1.01% and 21.59% for LSTM and CNN respectively.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence for Face recognition and Assistance for Visually Impaired
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: In this world, many people are affected by blindness and they face so many difficulties in their daily life. According to World Health Organization (WHO), there are approximately 2.2 billion people who are completely blind. They need to depend on primitive solutions like white canes, trained dogs, or other people. But these helping hands cannot always assist them. The affected people need a smart assisting device that avoids bumping into an obstacle and helps in navigating from one place to another independently. This proposed work describes the smart walking stick which makes blind people walk safely. By using the latest technologies and IoT devices, this smart walking stick can be developed where it provides safe navigation to the user. The proposed system employs a novel solution for navigation in indoor with the help of deep learning algorithms. In case of panic situations or emergency conditions, the predefined message with the user's location will be sent to the caretaker using an API. This smart walking stick is affordable, durable and provides more convenience to the user to walk safely, and gives more confidence without depending on any other externals.

articleTitle: Development of IoT Based Home Automation System Using Smartphone
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: The main aim of this study is to make an IOT-based home automation system utilizing a Wi-Fi based microcontroller. It is quite beneficial in leading a comfortable and high-quality lifestyle. A smartphone with an Android app for managing electrical household appliances. We used Node MCU(Esp8266), Wi-Fi module, Relay, IoT, smartphone, and other electrical components in this study. The benefits of this project include the ability to handle all our household appliances from a single location, which saves time and provides comfort. It is extremely advantageous to physically challenged and disabled individuals. It improves energy efficiency and is ideal for energy conservation. It is fast, dependable, and simple to use.

articleTitle: Solar Irradiation Forecast Enhancement Using Hybrid Architecture
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Power balancing at the grid is much more involved process due to the fact that solar power generation is primarily weather dependent, as it is relied on solar irradiation, which is very volatile and unpredictable. Accurate solar irradiation forecasting can significantly increase the performance of solar power plants. This research is motivated by the current advancements in deep learning (DL) models and its practical use in the green energy field. The proposed model combines two DL architectures: convolutional neural network (CNN) and long short-term memory (LSTM). The effectiveness of the same is analysed by comparing with recurrent neural network (RNN) family architectures. The RNN family models are Long Short Term Memory (LSTM), Bi-directional LSTM (Bi-LSTM), Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), and Bi-directional GRU (Bi-GRU). The simulations are conducted on a publicly available data set from Desert Knowledge Australia Solar Centre (DKASC), Australia. A meteorological station across the Northern Territory (NT Solar resource) collects high resolution solar and climate data from Darwin location, which is used for the experiment. From the results, it is evident that each of the bidirectional model outperform its unidirectional equivalent architectures. However, the hybrid network (CNN-LSTM) outperforms all the individual models as per the error metric analysis.

articleTitle: Butterfly Optimisation of MPPT for Solar PV under Shading Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: The most prevalent and cleanest source of solar-derived electricity is provided by photovoltaic systems. The P-V and I-V characteristics of the Photovoltaic (PV) system show how several peaks are created when there is partial shadowing. Because of various peaks, variations, and sluggish power tracking speeds, Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) algorithms are unable to reach the worldwide peak power. The Butterfly Optimisation Algorithm (BOA), a unique metaheuristic method for extracting global maxima from shaded panels, is presented in this paper. The main objective is to use BOA to quickly and accurately trace the Maximum Power Point (MPP) of the Solar Photovoltaic system under irregular shading situations. For each PV array configuration, BOA-based simulation results for three alternative shading patterns (such as 4P1S, 4P3S, and 4P2S) are tested against the PSO, Cuckoo Search, and Grey Wolf Optimisation algorithms. A PV module, DC-DC Boost Converter, and the load are all included in the modelling of the PV array in MATLAB/Simulink. The simulation results show that the BOA approach is more effective and has a faster tracing speed when the various algorithms are contrasted to the suggested algorithm.

articleTitle: Transient Stability Improvement of the DFIG-Based Wind Turbine Using Adaptive Controlled STATCOM
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: In this paper, a new approach is presented that utilizes a least mean square root of exponential (LMSRE)-based adaptive filtering algorithm to enhance the transient stability of doubly fed induction generator (DFIG) based wind turbines through the static synchronous compensator (STATCOM). The control strategy of the STATCOM relies on the voltage source converter (VSC). The proposed method involves the online adjustment of the gain of all the proportional-integral (PI) controllers in the VSC's cascaded structure using the LMSRE algorithm, which ensures rapid convergence. The selection of the LMSRE algorithm in this study is motivated by its quick convergence rate, minimum computational intricacy, and straightforward structure. To assess the effectiveness of the proposed LMSRE-PI based adaptive controlled STATCOM, its performance is compared with a PI controller based on the least mean square (LMS) adaptive algorithm under symmetrical voltage sag conditions. The effectiveness of the proposed adaptive controlled STATCOM is verified through the utilization of MATLAB/Simulink software, thereby validating its performance.

articleTitle: Analysis of Processor Execution Time in Modeling DC-DC Converters For Mild Hybrid Electric Vehicle Application
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Electric Vehicles (EVs) have gained popularity in recent years due to higher efficiency and lesser pollution. EVs mainly contain converters (DC-DC and DC-AC) for voltage regulation and controlled power flow. Buck and Boost converters are popular converters that are used in 48V Mild Hybrid EV applications. In this work, the time taken by the Central Processing Unit (CPU) to provide the inductor current and the output voltage values for an ideal and practical buck and boost converters operating in Continuous Conduction Mode (CCM) is found Tic and Toc commands using MATLAB 2018A and 2021B versions using Ordinary Differential Equation (ODE) and Symbolic Expression (SYMS) solvers. It is found that the ODE solver provides a faster response as it uses numerical techniques to solve the coupled governing equations. Though the versions of the software are different, CPU execution time remains unchanged for ODE solvers.

articleTitle: Optimized Power Scheduling in Microgrids Under Load Uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Microgrid is a controllable system that supplies power generated from some distributed units operating in an islanded or grid-connected mode to a community load. Renewable energy sources are beneficial to microgrids for clean energy generation. This paper proposes a memory-based multi-verse optimization (MMVO) algorithm for optimal power scheduling in microgrids among various generation units under load uncertainty. The random nature of the uncertain load is modeled using stochastic programming, and the improved algorithm is tested on two different scale microgrids, i.e., IEEE 37 -node and IEEE 141-node test systems. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm minimizes the energy production cost under uncertain load demand.

articleTitle: A Study of Galfenol-Based Magnetostrictive Energy Harvester Under Different Vibrations
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: When an external magnetic field is applied to a ferromagnetic material like Galfenol, Terfenol-D, etc., they generally tend to expand or contract. This property of the materials is known as magnetostriction. Magnetostrictive materials thereby convert the applied electromagnetic energy into harness able mechanical energy and can be utilized in various applications. The Villari effect or the inverse magnetostrictive effect is just the opposite of Joule's effect of magnetostriction. It refers to the phenomenon in which the application of external stress causes a change in the magnetic domains of the materials and thus an electromotive force is generated in the material. In other words, in inverse magnetostriction, the mechanical energy thus gets converted to electromagnetic energy. This electromagnetic energy or rather the voltage obtained is put to various other applications such as a source of self-sustained power supply of wireless sensor networks especially in harsh and hostile environments. Also, it can be said that this effect of inverse magnetostriction is related to ambient vibrations and thus can also to put to various practical uses such as the health monitoring of civil structures. But for putting the magnetostrictive energy sensors in that use, it's important to decide which of the parameters between voltage and frequency can be the deciding factor. The paper tries to find out the same by the application of various hardware equipment and understanding the relation.

articleTitle: Design of a PV-Integrated EV Charging Station with Power Management Schemes
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Here, the proposed work primarily focused on the planning of a grid-connected electric vehicle (EV) charging station integrated with a solar photovoltaic (PV) system. The foremost objective of the paper is to investigate the feasibility of utilizing renewable energy sources to charge EVs and to reduce the dependency on non-renewable energy sources. A multi-level constant current (MLCC) charging technique for EVs was implemented by considering the different states of charge (SOC) of EV batteries. Also, a constant DC bus voltage regulation-based power management scheme was implemented for optimal utilization of the sources and optimal sharing of active power. The control technique for the proposed PV-integrated EV charging station was verified through MATLAB/Simulink results and OPAL-RT experimental results.

articleTitle: Design of E-Bike Swapping Station and its Impact Analysis on LV Power Distribution System
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: The electric bike (E-bike) market is growing rapidly year by year, the total number of electric bike sales in the year 2017 was just 1515 and in 2022 it become 6,15,365, which means approx. 406% increment has been recorded. Though it is good for the green environment, charging these bikes is becoming another challenge. It is creating a huge burden on the distribution line as most people are preferring home charging. These E-bike loads are the extra loads on the grid, and in the future, they may create a huge disturbance in the power system. So, it is very important to be prepared for the future challenge and try to overcome the problems. In this regard, we must know the impact of these E-bike loads on the system. In this paper the analysis of the impact of the E-bike load is done which will help to overcome the system instability problem along with that it will also help in achieving uninterrupted power supply to the household and industries even after supplying the E-bike loads. Voltage instability is the main issue of the distribution system so this analysis is also considered here.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Coil Voltage of a Galfenol-based Energy Harvester by Dimension Modification
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: With the increasing demand for clean energy and a good reliable form of energy, magnetostrictive energy harvesters have continuously developed, which derive energy from ambient vibrations. A perpetual source of electrical energy can be extracted from structural vibrations. This sensor is made up of Gallium (Ga) and Iron (Fe) alloy and allows it to generate electrical energy from structural vibration. This paper deals with a comparative study of different sizes of stainless steel, Galfenol, and their respective output voltages. The goal of this paper is to find an efficient configuration for a sensor. In order to evaluate the performance of the proposed design, we conduct various simulations for various dimensions of a prototype using COMSOL Multiphysics.

articleTitle: Power Quality Control and Comparison of a Micro Grid System Using Fuzzy MPPT Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: This paper presents a power quality control in a microgrid system using different Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) techniques. The main aim of the study is to evaluate the performance of the microgrid system in terms of power quality parameters, such as harmonic distortion and voltage stability, when different MPPT techniques are employed. The microgrid system incorporates a hybrid power generation system consisting of solar panels, wind turbines, and energy storage systems, which are integrated and controlled using different MPPT techniques, including the Perturb & Observation (P&O) method and the Fuzzy MPPT technique. A single-phase sinusoidal pulse width modulation (SPWM) inverter, based on the PQ control strategy, is used to supply power to the grid and maintain a constant DC link voltage. Additionally, a fuel cell is employed to substantially reduce power fluctuations. A comparison of the power quality performance of the micro grid system using these MPPT techniques is carried out through simulation studies using MATLAB/Simulink platform. The results are analyzed and discussed in detail, and recommendations are provided for improving the power quality control of the microgrid system.

articleTitle: Smart Control Strategy for a DC Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: DC microgrids are widely used as most of the renewable sources generate power in DC and they are superior to AC micro grids in view of control, efficiency and number of conversion stages. Design and control of a basic DC micro grid is the primary objective of the present work. For that a DC micro grid consisting of PV generation unit, wind energy conversion unit, battery storage unit and grid interfacing unit is designed in MATLAB/Simulink. A voltage source inverter for utility interface, a DC-DC bidirectional converter to interface with battery, a rectifier and boost converter combination for wind system interface and a MPPT controlled boost converter for solar unit interface have been used. Lead acid battery is used as an energy storing unit, interfaced with the DC bus using a bidirectional DC-DC converter. For both charging and discharging mode of operation, control strategies have been developed and implemented. The grid interfacing converter is modelled in synchronous rotating reference frame under balanced load conditions. To control the rectifier, voltage- oriented control scheme in dq reference frame has been utilized. Phase locked loop was implemented for grid synchronization.

articleTitle: Protection Coordination Scheme in Microgrid with Common Optimal Settings of User-Defined Dual-Setting Overcurrent Relays
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: The changing amplitude and direction of short circuit current in the islanded mode (IM) and grid-connected mode (GM) make microgrid protection a significant problem. As relay coordination depends upon the fault current level, therefore, two different relay settings are required for proper coordination among relay pairs, one for each operating mode. Further, the performance of the coordination scheme depends upon the types of relays. In this context, this paper proposes a modified protection coordination scheme for microgrids by considering the user-defined dual setting directional overcurrent relays (DS-DOCRs) capable of providing coordination in both IM and GM. The main objective of the study is to determine the common optimal relay settings i.e., time multiplier setting (TMS), plug setting (PS) and relay characteristics constants (α) that can provide satisfactory coordination in each operating mode. The proposed approach is tested on a 7-bus microgrid (low voltage part of IEEE-14 bus system) and genetic algorithm (GA) is used as an optimization tool to determine the optimal relay settings.

articleTitle: Study on Performance of 100KW Grid-Connected Rooftop Solar Power Generation at BCE Bhagalpur, India
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: At present when the whole world is reeling under extreme levels of pollution, India has started investing rigorously in expanding its renewable energy generation capacity. Bihar being one of the most populous and power deficit regions in the country has also undertaken the job of expanding the horizons of its renewable energy generation through Bihar Renewable Energy Development Authority (BREDA). BREDA has installed a 100kW Grid-connected solar power plant at Bhagalpur College of Engineering (BCE), Bhagalpur located in the eastern Bihar. This paper has discussed the design layout, procedure and economics of the 100kW power plant installed at BCE Bhagalpur. The plant is expected to generate almost 135,000 kWh per annum and keeping this and the losses in mind it will lead to reduction of about 75-80% of electricity bill of BCE Bhagalpur. By the end of 5 years, the plant will pay back the investment done on the installation and from sixth year it will start generating profit for the college. Ultimately this plant will pave way for further infrastructure expansion in the college like EV charging station, new academic and co-curricular buildings, etc. Hence this paper has tried to throw some light on the benefits of solar power plants which can prove useful for further capacity expansion of the solar power plant at BCE Bhagalpur and other government buildings in Bihar.

articleTitle: NFT based Green Energy and Assets Trading Application over Decentralized Marketplace
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Digital decentralized marketplace is now becoming more popular since 2015 due to invention of NFT technology. NFT is most successfully implemented in digital contents like art and music and is evolving as a new market for the future. NFT and its underlying technology blockchain is now being diversified into various application areas to solve various requirement of human and its society. In the current global scenario green house effect and its solution though alternating energy sources like renewable energy generation is major challenge due to distributed nature of these sources. Moreover, establishment of such infrastructure need much investments. Distributed management using blockchain technology is the only solution to manage energy generation and exchange between prosumer and consumer. However, to achieve net zero emission (NZE) we need much more investment in the clean energy sector and is not possible unless more and more people join and participate in the investment. This study proposes a new solution for secure and intelligent trading of solar charging stations and electric vehicle equipment in a decentralized digital marketplace, utilizing NFT technology. The approach is designed to improve the reliability and transparency of transactions, providing a more secure and efficient system for trading these valuable assets.

articleTitle: Impact of Multiple Time Varying Delay on the Stability of Load Frequency Control System with EV Aggregator
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: In this paper, the work deals with the impact of multiple time varying delay on the stability of load frequency control (LFC) system when the electric vehicle aggregator (EVA) is involved. The utilisation of communication links for sharing of the information between different sub-systems generates unavoidable time delays. Time varying delays have a significant impact on the stability of the system. So, the LFC system's stability analysis is carried out while taking EVA into consideration. The LMI framework is used in this study to ensure the system's asymptotic stability. The delay dependent criterion employed in this work is based on the Lyapunov theory and Wirtinger based integral inequality.

articleTitle: Demodulation-Based Spectral Analysis of Input Current with Gabor Transform in Detection of Electrical Faults in Induction Motors
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: In this paper, detection of electrical faults in a Three Phase Induction Motor (TPIM) using current spectral analysis (CSA) is presented. Induction motors are main workhorse of many industries due to their advent features like robust construction, wide range of control and cost effective etc. Due to huge usage of these machines without monitoring, they face unexpected failures. These faults cause motors to abruptly stop, resulting in unexpected downtime for production and revenue. It is highly undesirable and imposes continuous monitoring of these faults in early stage. Electrical faults require special attention among the various faults encountered by induction motors due to their abrupt consequences on machine performance. On the other hand, CSA is a more widely used fault monitoring technique than other methods such as vibration, noise, temperature, and chemical parameters. Conventional CSA using Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) has many issues and are addressed using proposed Gabor Transform (G T) and the noise due to acquisition of input current is removed using demodulation. The fault severity of proposed electrical faults is estimated using selected feature parameters. The proposed fault detection topology is examined experimentally using 2 HP, 440 V, and 50 Hz three phase induction motor using LabView and MATLAB environment.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Control of Islanded DC Microgrid with SOC-based Power Sharing
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: In this paper, the solar PV-fed DC microgrid with several battery energy storage systems (BESS) is proposed to be equipped with a power-sharing scheme (PSS). The finite control set-model predictive control is implemented for the charging/discharging control of BESS. The PV system is operated in maximum power point tracking (MPPT) mode. As solar irradiance has intermittent nature, the power output of the PV fluctuates. The BESS is vital for maintaining power balance and DC bus voltage stability. The BESS must be operated within its SOC limits to prevent overcharging or deep discharging. In the proposed PSS, the centralized controller considers the SOC of each battery bank for power-sharing among the BESSs. Load shading and dump loads schemes are also incorporated in the PSS. The experimental verification of the proposed power-sharing scheme was carried out in MATLAB/Simulink and the results indict the effectiveness of the PSS. Experimental verification for the proposed PSS is carried out using hardware in the loop.

articleTitle: Decentralized PID-Based Sliding Mode Load Frequency Control Scheme in Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: In this paper, a decentralized PID-sliding mode controller is designe for load frequency control (LFC) of multi-area power system with both matched as well as unmatched uncertainties. In the design of the sliding mode control approach, a PID sliding surface is considered, and based on the reaching law, a robust controller is designed to ensure that the frequency and tie-line power deviations converge to zero after different load perturbations are given in each area. The required stability condition is established using Lyapunov's stability theorem and verifies the implied controller's reliability. To validate the proposed controller design, Matlab environment is used for carrying out simulations under various conditions. The obtained results convey that the decentralized PID-sliding mode control ensures stable operation of the three area power system and can achieve the desired goal with less overshoot in finite time.

articleTitle: Implementation of a blockchain based DApp for P2P electricity trading
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: This article details the implementation of a decentralized application (DApp) based on public blockchain Ethereum for token backed P2P electricity trading, with electric vehicle as one the peers. A hybrid market model with a peer matching mechanism with score-based peer matching orchestrated by smart contracts is used and results are presented. Solidity language is used to create smart contracts which runs on the top of open source Ethereum public blockchain. Lockable tokens are created by modifying ERC20 APIs with wallets deployed using MetaMask. Client-side programming with Node-Express with a user interface is deployed. Truffle suite-based unit testing of whole DApp is carried out and deployed to block chain. The cost analysis for deployment of DApp both the simulation environment Ganache and test network Goerli is also presented with cost allocation to different market players.

articleTitle: Coordinate Scheduling of Plug-in Electric Vehicles at Charging Station Fed by Renewable Energy Sources
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Utilizing renewable energy sources (RES) simultaneously eliminates the need for an energy storage system (ESS), reducing overall cost. This research paper focuses on developing an algorithm for efficiently scheduling electric vehicles (EVs) charging at a charging station. The Monte Carlo Method has been used to generate the arrival times of EVs at the station for each time slot. The algorithm consists of two main components: The Vehicle Acceptance Algorithm (VAA) and the Vehicle Scheduling Algorithm (VSA). Accepted vehicles can engage in Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) charging once their State of Charge (SOC) reaches a certain level. Renewable power is supplied through a combination of solar and wind energy. Upon arrival at the charging station, EVs are scheduled based on the available energy at that particular time slot, which includes the remaining energy from RES, the V2V energy of previously scheduled vehicles, and the charger's availability. In cases where there is an energy shortage during a timeslot, EV owners can charge their vehicles using grid power. In order to promote social welfare among EV owners who prefer charging with RES, certain incentives are provided alongside the low cost of charging from renewable sources.

Author Keywords: Reduction of burden from the grid

articleTitle: Adaptive Noise Cancellation Technique in Signal Estimation using Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Noise is one of the most hindering factors in signal processing as they are random in nature, and it may obliterate the signal of interest. Noise may arise due to errors in the sensor as well as erroneous transmission channels. These errors are inherent in real-world applications and may cause errors in measuring quantity. In our proposed model, Particle Swarm Optimization PSO is used to optimize the adaptive filter coefficients of an Adaptive line enhancer (ALE) to remove the noise from the received signal. The proposed PSO based ALE is designed in MATLAB, and its performance is investigated for different scenarios.

Author Keywords: Particle Swarm Optimization PSO. Adaptive filter

articleTitle: Backstepping Controller Design for Maximum Power Harvesting from Solar-Wind Hybrid Energy Conversion System
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Renewable energy sources are essential in the battle against escalating dangers associated with climate change and global warming. Among these resources, wind and solar energy are readily available and frequently used. An effective approach to harnessing these sources involves integrating a wind energy conversion system (WECS) and a solar energy conversion system (SECS) and utilizing the combined output to supply the grid. This paper presents a backstepping controller to maximize the power transfer from this hybrid system to the grid. The proposed controller enables the fast realization of the maximum power point (MPP), resulting in grid-side total harmonic distortion (THD) below 5%. The results are simulated in MATLAB/Simulink to demonstrate the system's effectiveness.

articleTitle: Francis turbine control with electrohydraulic inlet guide vane system dynamics
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Francis turbine (FT) system dynamics include water flow nonlinearities, a generator, and an electrohydraulic inlet guide vane system making a complicated system. Most of the previous research did not include the dynamics of the electrohydraulic inlet guide vane (IGV) system and detailed flow analysis for FT system studies. The present work considers detailed dynamics of water flow through FT system, IGV and its actuation system. The velocity diagram approach has been considered based on Euler's equation of FT to capture water flow dynamics through the FT. The model integrated with the electrohydraulic inlet guide vane system dynamic model with the consideration of the effect of inlet guide vane angular position (IGVAP) on flow loss hence power loss. Further, the generator dynamics also has been integrated with the FT system model. The proposed model has been validated with the experimental result of a Lab. scale experimental setup. The controller design is based on the consideration of the IGV position error and FT speed error. A fuzzy feedforward-PID bias controller has been developed to control efficiently under various external disturbances. Performance comparison of PID, PID feedforward (PIDF), fuzzy PID feedforward (F-PIDF) and fuzzy PID feedforward bias (F-PIDFB) controllers have been studied for the FT system control application. The controller performances have been studied with water head disturbance with a sinusoidal signal

articleTitle: Overlapping FSS-Based Energy-Efficient Routing in Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Forwarding Search Space (FSS) in position-based routing for Wireless Sensor Networks (WSN) controls unneces-sary transmissions, thereby balancing the sensor nodes' energy consumption. This research article aims to improve energy efficiency by considering the overlapping Forwarding Search Space (FSS) of two nodes simultaneously sending data to the base station. The article first introduces a mathematical model to represent the problem scenario. It then presents simulation results demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed mecha-nism and other existing methods in reducing transmissions and balancing energy consumption among sensor nodes. The study considers metrics such as nodes in FSS, number of dead nodes, network lifetime, and number of messages for evaluating the performance of these methods.

articleTitle: An Inductive Wireless Charging Solution For Underwater Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Various unmanned underwater machines are increasingly used for undersea exploration, especially the autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs). The AUVs can operate in inaccessible areas which include under the ice, deep oceans, and military zones. They spend longer duration underwater which leads to depletion of battery charge. Charging of batteries is one of the challenges that AUV s face. The conventional methods adopted to keep the system powered are battery swapping and direct electric charging (DEC) techniques. Battery swapping is frequently time-consuming, the DEC requires extremely precise alignment and corrosion and biofouling pose a risk to the system's integrity. With a significant degree of misalignment between the coils, inductive wireless power transfer (IWPT) solutions are more secure, practical, dependable, and effective. The conductivity and separation between the coils greatly affect the optimum frequency for efficient power transfer. This work proposes inductive wireless power transfer and recharging solutions for underwater vehicles which are automatically tuned to the optimum frequency of power transfer with good quality(Q) factor.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of a Permanent Magnetic Fault Current Limiter at Various Supply Voltages
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: In this era, with the development of technology and with the increase of population the demand for power and energy is increasing day by day. This results in the increase of fault current levels. To cope up with this increased fault current, Fault Current Limiter (FCL) is a viable solution. FCL can be used for any voltage level. The FCL used for operation, in this paper, is fabricated for low voltage operation. A Permanent Magnet Fault Current Limiter (PMFCL) is used. The model is simulated on ANSYS and the fabricated hardware is run at different voltage levels. This research provides a detailed analysis of the PMFCL's operation under various power input conditions.

articleTitle: Wavelet Transform Based Data Processing Technique for Solar and Wind Energy Forecasting Using Auto Regressive Integrated Moving Average Model
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: To reduce the detrimental effect of conventional generators on environment, almost all modern power systems are integrated with renewable energy sources (RES). The two most popular RES for power systems, among the various ones that are available, are solar photovoltaic (PV) and wind energy conversion systems (WECS). Although solar PV and WECS are most popular RES, the intermittency of solar irradiation and wind speed leads towards difficulty in energy management of a microgrid. Therefore, proper forecasting of solar PV and WECS generation is very important for operation of microgrid integrated with RES. An autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) model based machine learning method is presented in this paper to forecast the output power of solar PV and WECS based power generation. The forecasting was developed based on solar irradiation data and wind speed of a location. The output from autoregressive integrated moving average model is further compared with moving average (MA) and simple exponential smoothing (SES) model. The effectiveness of the ARIMA model is verified using mean error (ME), mean absolute error (MAE) and mean square error (MSE).

articleTitle: Design and Modelling of a PV Based Electric Vehicle Charging System
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: The adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) has been increasing rapidly in the recent years. However, the challenging issues is to develop one reliable, convenient, and sustainable charging station, To overcome this challenge, in this paper a Photo Voltaic (PV) based EV charging system has been developed. The proposed system utilizes the solar energy as the main source of power to the on-grid EV charging station operating in a bi-directional mode, to ensure the uninterrupted and reliable charging of all the components associated with the system such as the DC-DC converter, DC-AC inverter, and the control system for regulating the charging process, it is connected to the grid. The performance of the proposed charging station is evaluated under different scenarios, including variations in solar irradiance and EV charging demand, separate controller scheme has been implemented in PV array with boost converter and EV with bidirectional converter, the reference signal generation is carried out using dual PQ based control technique, the effectiveness of the controller used in this work is verified through MATLAB Simulink

articleTitle: BASB-SG: A Biohashing-based Authentication Scheme for Secure Blockchain-enabled Smart Grids
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Smart grids offer several uses and advantages that make them a compelling technology for modern power systems. They provide improved reliability and efficiency and reduce cost and energy consumption while also integrating renewable energy sources. Authentication is crucial in smart grid security to ensure that only authorized parties can access the system's resources. However, most authentication mechanisms used in the past are computationally intensive and may not be appropriate for devices with limited resources. To address this challenge, we propose a secure smart grid authentication mechanism using blockchain technology and biohashing to verify smart meters to a service agency. Thus, enabling smart meters to access services such as electricity consumption reports and feedback in a secure manner. We perform an analysis and compare BASB-SG with other works in the same field to prove that BASB-SG guarantees better security while remaining lightweight which makes it ideal to use in real-world smart grids.

articleTitle: Classification of Micro-Moment-Based Anomalous Power Consumption Using Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: The identification of unusual power usage in buildings is crucial for improving energy efficiency. Using an electrical consumption monitoring system can help with energy conservation by identifying unusual energy consumption patterns. This paper suggests a micro-moment-based methodology for detecting abnormal power use. This study makes use of a benchmark dataset called SimDataset, which is used in most of the micro-moment classification-related works. On the images created from the dataset labeled with two classes and five classes, binary and multi-class classifications have both been used. Transfer learning is used by employing pre-trained CNN models, namely DenseNet121, ResNet50V2, and Xception model. The results depicted that the DenseNet121 model has outperformed all other models by giving the best accuracy of 99% and F1-score of 0.984.

articleTitle: Power Converter Design for Fuel Cell Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Renewable, readily available and reduced emissions are the maj or driving elements for adopting fuel cell as clean and substitute power source today. Nonetheless, the high costs of the fuel cell systems make it hard to analyse its behaviour for different applications and real-time testing. In the field of renewable energy, fuel cell technology and power converter play a vital role. Hence, a highly efficient power converter is an essential requirement for such type of application. To address this issue, the paper proposes a fuel cell model and a power converter design with PI controller ensuring a constant output voltage at different loading conditions as well as varying operating temperatures. The modelling of fuel cell is carried out in Python. The fuel cell model is verified for A vista SR-12 500W fuel cell stack parameters. Fuel cell behaviour is studied through the proposed Python model, being the open-source software and its combination with MATLAB for designing DC-DC converter makes it easy to collaboratively work over both the platforms. Thus, the study encourages the ongoing energy transformation by promoting fuel cells: the green and clean source of energy.

articleTitle: IOT Based Automation of Pre-treatment Plant for Surface Coating with Multiple Batch System
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Powder Coating is a method of applying decorative and protective finish to a wide range of materials and products that are used by both industries and consumers. Pre-Treatment is a process that manufactures need to go through to remove all grease, oils and dirt from the metal (usually conductive) surfaces. The process of pre-treatment has the following stages: Degreasing, Derusting, Phosphating, Passivation and Water Rinsing. Depending on the type of material that is to be pre-treated, the stages of the pre-treatment cycle can be varied accordingly. The existing system lacks in modes and in efficiency due to the inability for simultaneous execution. The pre-treatment process can be operated in three modes: Automatic, Manual and Maintenance. The system is a multiple batch system that allows multiple trays (batches) to be treated simultaneously with the help of electromagnetic latching mechanism. Integrating the system with lOT removes the restriction of localized operation and allows the operator to control the entire system remotely, without being present on the assembly floor. Further the quality of the proposed system is evaluated using Analytic Hierarchy Process(AHP).

articleTitle: Ultrasonic Vibration Parameters Estimation using Fuzzy based PID Controller in Digital-PLL
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Ultrasonic vibration parameters are estimated using a Fuzzy based Phase locked loop. A quadrature detector based on the modified sliding discrete Fourier transform (SDFT) is employed that acts as a band-pass filter. A damping factor (r) is introduced in the SDFT to ensure the stability of the filter. Complex poles are eliminated by rationalizing the SDFT filter known as the Goertzel algorithm. The quadrature phase of the Goertzel filter is then passed through a low pass filter. The output of the low pass filter contains the vibration information along with noise. To eliminate the noise, a Fuzzy based PID controller is employed. This fuzzy system, when coupled with the PID controller, is able to estimate a wide range of vibrating frequencies. The output of the PID controller is then fed to a bi-quad oscillator that produces variable pulses, which ensures the phase-locking mechanism. This nonlinear Fuzzy based PID controller can replace the tedious manual tuning procedure. Simulation results validate the efficient performance of the proposed PLL in dynamic and noisy environments.

articleTitle: A Quadratic High Step-Up Interleaved Converter with Coupled Inductor for Renewable Energy Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: This paper presents a high gain DC-DC configuration using coupled inductor and voltage multiplier circuit suitable for PV application. In order to reduce the current stress at the input side, the interleaved configuration is used at the input. The voltage multiplier circuit not only ensures the high voltage gain but also provides an effective clamping of the switch voltage stress. The proposed configuration achieves a high reduction in the switch voltage stress compared to the similar configurations with a high gain structure. The proposed configuration is presented with the comparison of voltage gains, and active switch stress levels across the switches for similar topologies. The converter input current is continuous and due to interleaved configuration along with quadratic boost configuration, the input side inductance is decreased. The various modes of operation of the converter and the simulation results are presented.

articleTitle: Data Analytics for Core Temperature Estimation in Battery Management System for Electric and Hybrid Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Compared to conventional means of transport thatuse fossil fuels, electric vehicles are known to reduce pollution levels as they take power from renewable sources of energy stored in energy storage devices like batteries and fuel cells. Core temperature estimation of batteriesis extremely important inbattery management systems for preventing thermal runaway and ensuring safe operation. In this study, core temperature is estimated using a Kalman filter for two different battery chemistries viz; lithium polymer and lithium iron phosphate using a second-order thermal model. Further, a linear regression model is applied to verify the prediction over the trained and tested dataset. The lithium iron phosphate prediction curvehad a fit of approximately 82-83%, whilelithium polymerhad a fit of 72-82% during the charging and discharging of OCV-SOC variation.

articleTitle: Design of SMES for Load Frequency Control in Power Systems with Renewable Integration
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: The growing utilization of renewable energy resources and the increasing electricity demand pose significant challenges in ensuring the reliability and security of interconnected power systems. Due to the intermittent nature of renewable energy source, maintaining system frequency within acceptable limits becomes crucial to ensure reliable operation and control of power system. However, mitigating frequency deviations and keeping them within specified limit is a complex task. This paper suggest an SMES system for improving the stability via ALFC in two area power system. The control objective is to regulate the load frequency error of the power system under various load changes.
