The SMES system is added into a two thermal area power system which includes reheat and non-reheat turbines. The simulation includes external disturbances and load variations. The simulation results demonstrate the significant reduction in parameters such as settling time and peak value, indicating the effectiveness of the SMES in enhancing system performance and stability.

articleTitle: Capacitor Trapped Current Fed ZCS-ZVS Push Pull DC-DC converter for renewable energy conversion
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: A current fed ZCS-ZVS push-pull converter has been analyzed and designed for renewable energy conversion applications. The topology maintains both zero current switching (ZCS) and (ZVS) on leading and trailing edges owing to the resonance between the trapped capacitor and the leakage inductance of the HF transformer, resulting in a near sinusoidal waveform at the primary of the HF transformer. The voltage spike across the power devices are suppressed effectively enabling the selection of low-voltage, low cost power devices. The proposed converter no auxiliary circuit is involved and since all the switches are ground referred, non-isolated driver with single power supply can be employed. A comprehensive study of 500 W highly efficient push pull converter and design of the proposed converter including steady-state and transient analysis has been reported.

articleTitle: A Novel FWHT-GPR based Fault Location Scheme for TCSC-compensated Transmission Line
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel fault location scheme for transmission lines equipped with thyristor-controlled series compensators (TCSCs). The proposed method combines the FWHT and the GPR techniques to estimate the fault distance accurately. The FWHT is used to transform the measured current and voltage signals into the frequency domain, while GPR is used to model the relationship between the fault distance and the transformed signals. The proposed scheme has been tested using simulation studies, and the results show that it can accurately locate the fault distance for different fault types and fault locations, even in the presence of TCSCs. The proposed scheme can also handle noise and measurement errors effectively. The proposed FWHT-GPR based fault location scheme can be used as a reliable tool for the protection of TCSC-compensated transmission lines.

articleTitle: Microgrid Protection using Empirical Mode Decomposition and MRMR Feature Ranking Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Microgrid deployment has increased significantly in recent years due to the advantages of supplying load locally with increased reliability. However, the intermittent nature of renewables and presence of bi-directional power, and various modes of operation constitute different set of protection problems. This article presents a novel approach to microgrid protection using empirical mode decomposition (EMD) signal processing and minimum redundancy maximum relevance (MRMR) feature ranking coupled with k-nearest neighbor (KNN) classification. The proposed methodology leverages EMD to decompose the voltage and current signals into intrinsic mode functions (IMFs), which are then ranked using MRMR algorithm to select the most relevant features. KNN is then employed for fault detection and classification. The proposed method has been tested on a modified IEEE 13-bus distribution microgrid and performance indices validate the effectiveness of the proposed methodology in detecting and classifying faults.

articleTitle: Distributed Control for Accurate Voltage/Frequency Regulation and Power Sharing in a Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Owing to uncertainties arising from the intermittent nature of distributed generating resources, communication constraints, and parameter variations in the dynamics, control of a microgrid is challenging. This paper presents the design of a multi-agent-based distributed adaptive controller for a microgrid. The paper presents the design of an adaptive controller to regulate the voltage and frequencies of the distributed generating sources at nominal values in the face of the uncertainties mentioned above. The MG setup consists of four distributed generating (DG) sources of 35kW each. The performance of the proposed distributed controller is compared with a secondary voltage controller [14] by pursuing simulations using MATLAB/Simulink and then in real-time using OPAL-RT. The simulation and experimental analysis envisage that the proposed controller exhibits faster convergence and handles sudden load change and plug-and-play operations compared to the secondary voltage controller.

articleTitle: Electrical Distance Based ML-Assisted Clustering Case Study on Indian 62-Bus Utility Grid for Voltage Control Area Determination
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Managing the ever-increasing power demand through a complex electrical grid, fulfilling all physical and economic constraints, is a challenge to grid operators. Supplying stable, reliable and resilient power often necessitates partitioning of the power grid for easy and flexible control. One of the critical aspects of grid management is voltage control through proper reactive power management. Using the already established concept of electrical distance, a framework is given to form a voltage control area through the machine learning method of hierarchical clustering. The case study on the Indian 62-bus utility system establishes the feasibility of such a clustering algorithm.

articleTitle: Integration of AGC and Real-Time Energy Market Model in Power Systems for Dynamic Performance Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: This paper studies real-time balancing of generation and load demand using discrete automatic generation control (AGC) and dynamic real-time energy market (RTEM) model. It is assumed that the RTEM model has a short dispatch trading period of 5 minutes which is somehow comparable with a discrete AGC system. Two different test systems i.e., two-area and three- area systems in the presence of AGC and RTEM model are considered to investigate the dynamic performance. Penetration of renewable energy sources such as photovoltaic and wind units is considered as a part of conventional AGC units as well as the RTEM model. It is found that contributions from both AGC and RTEM models improve the dynamic response of the power systems overall by minimizing the frequency and tie-line power deviations.

articleTitle: Bearing Fault Detection in Induction Motor using Ensemble Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Most industrial applications are powered by rotating equipment that is electrically driven. Due to its durability, effectiveness, and safety, the induction motor (IM) is the electrical machine that is employed the most in that situation. The emergence of an abrupt and unexpected defect might influence the induction motor (IM) operation, causing undesired disruptions that may cause significant stops in industrial processes despite its efficacy and dependability. Bearing failure, which accounts for around 40% of all faults, is the primary source of motor faults. This paper proposes an ensemble learning approach for the classification of bearing faults using vibration signals. The approach employs Random Forest, Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Artificial Neural Network (ANN) as base models and a gradient boosting classifier as the meta-learner. The study utilizes the dataset obtained from Case Western Reserve University and evaluates the proposed model's performance using various metrics, including accuracy, recall, precision and F1 scores. The proposed model achieved a high accuracy of 97.7<sup>%</sup>, demonstrating its superiority over individual base models. The outcomes show that the ensemble learning approach is useful for identifying bearing faults in industrial applications, offering a promising solution to enhance the reliability and efficiency of machinery systems. The research can contribute to improving the efficiency and reliability of such systems, leading to reduced downtime and maintenance costs.

articleTitle: BaTiO3 and ZnO-BaTiO3 Reinforced PVDF Flexible Capacitor for Microelectronic Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: The dielectric properties of barium titanate (BaTiO3) and Zinc oxide(ZnO) encapsulated in PVDF (Polyvinylidene fluoride) matrix were studied in a wide range of frequency(20 Hz to 1 MHz) and temperature(26 °C to 160 °C). Experimental evidences suggest that synergistic contribution of PVDF polymorphism and morphological features strongly affect the permittivity of the composite. ZnO decorated BaTiO3 particles in PVDF matrix has shown excellent dielectric properties with dielectric constant of 1.4<sup>x</sup>104, which is three order of magnitude higher than pristine PVDF. Conductivity of composites increases with the concentration of filler, they exhibit the negative temperature coefficient and the results are in good agreement with the Maxwell-Wagner model. The analysis sheds light on fabrication of high discharge energy density flexible capacitors for microelectronic devices.

articleTitle: Estimation of Dissipation Factor and Moisture Content of Kraft Paper Used in Transformer Bushing from Leakage Current
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: The bushing part of power transformers is usually exposed to very high electrical stress. This may cause unwanted failure, which will put the entire power distribution network at risk. The major part of the bushing insulation is comprised of oil-impregnated paper. A significant drawback of oil-paper insulation is that it accumulates moisture with service aging. High moisture content is also accompanied by high dielectric losses i.e. dielectric dissipation factor. This paper presents a method to predict moisture content and dissipation factor from leakage current data. Leakage current monitoring is a simple, low-complex monitoring method that can be used in online conditions. An attempt has been made in the present work to predict moisture content and dissipation factor from leakage current data. For this purpose, the harmonic content of the leakage current, especially the 3rd/7th harmonic ratio is the insulation-sensitive parameter.

articleTitle: Control and Analysis of a Grid connected Bi-Directional Converter-Inverter Interfaced Battery Energy Storage System
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: This paper presents a performance analysis and control of a grid connected battery energy system. A bidirectional DC-DC converter interfaced battery energy storage system is connected to a single-phase inverter to supply power to the grid / AC load or to receive power from the grid. In the control of the bi-directional DC-DC converter, a dual loop-control based on PI has been implemented. A vector control-based technique using the d-q transformation has been proposed for the single phase inverter control. In the DC-DC bidirectional converter control, it is observed that the converter's gain varies with the change in load resistance. However, gain becomes fixed after a certain value of load. The complete system is modelled using the dynamic equations and controllers are developed for both the single-phase inverter and DC-DC converter. The developed model is simulated in both the grid connected and isolated mode of operation with the help of MATLAB/Simulink. The results achieved are satisfactory and validate the working of the system.

articleTitle: Impact of Concentration Variations in P3HT: PCBM on Power Conversion Efficiency of Inverted Organic Solar Cell
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: In this paper, the solution dependent study on polymer: fullerene based bulk hetero-junction (BHJ) inverted organic solar cell (OSC) has been presented. It has been found that, in fabricated inverted OSC the power conversion efficiency (PCE) is strongly influenced by the weight ratio of donor and acceptor materials. Experimental results show that by modifying the weight ratio of poly (3-hexylthiophene) and phenyl C61 butyric acid methyl ester (P3HT: PCBM) in BHJ solution from 1.0:1.0 to 1.0:0.8, the PCE has been improved by ~40%. It has also been observed that, changes in blending ratio substantially increases the fill factor, open circuit voltage, and the short circuit current density of the device. Furthermore, with a weight ratio of 1.0:0.8, external quantum efficiency and the absorption spectrum also improves.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Regression Models for SoC Estimation in Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: This paper discusses the regression approach for predicting the State of Charge (SoC) of the battery in an Electric Vehicle (EV). During EV modelling, a Coulomb Counting Method (CCM) is employed to evaluate the SoC. The model is then developed and simulated in Matlab/Simulink under different drive cycles (FTP-75, HWFET, US06, and UDDS) to create datasets for the regression model training. Based on Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) value, a comparison of regression models reveals that neural networks provide better performance. The number of neurons that resulted in the lowest RMSE value turns out to be 15. The contributions are brief, as the ANN model's computational ability does not need a battery model and parameters and only desires current and voltage sensors. SoC is estimated using the developed regression model, and error is evaluated in comparison to the reference SoC was created using the CCM. The results show the developed model has an RMSE of 0.165, 0.7, 0.99, and 1.27 for neural network, ensemble bagged tree, SVM, and binary tree regression models, respectively, under the WLTP-3 drive cycle. Similarly, the RMSE turns out to be 0.127, 0.2984, 0.378, and 0.568 for neural network, SVM, ensemble bagged tree, and binary tree regressions, respectively under the LA-92 drive cycle.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of OMP and IGE OMP with Various Measurement Matrices in Compressive Sensing
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: As the name suggests, compressive sensing (CS) is a method that does compression while sampling. CS follows the Sub-Nyquist sampling process. Hence, it provides an advantage over sampling hardware complexity at higher frequencies and data transmission with fewer samples than traditional Shannon-Nyquist theory. The main challenge involved in CS is reconstructing original information using Sub-Nyquist samples at the receiver. To achieve this goal choosing an appropriate measurement matrix for a particular reconstruction algorithm is vital in this process. Incremental Gaussian Elimination (IGE) OMP reconstruction algorithm and Orthogonal Matching Pursuit (OMP) algorithms are considered in this work for reconstructing the original sinusoidal signal. And detailed performance analysis is conducted for different measurement matrices used in the IGE OMP and OMP reconstruction process.

articleTitle: Optimal Coordination of Over-current Relay Using KHO-KHO Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: The coordination of directional overcurrent relays (DOCRs) is a crucial aspect in ensuring the safety of the power system through the proper alignment of primary and backup protection systems. The goal of the coordination problem of overcurrent relays (OC) is to optimize the sum of the total operating time for all the main relays. The plug settings (PSs) and time dial settings (TDSs) play a crucial role in determining the operating time of relays. The challenge lies in the fact that the optimization model for this problem is non-linear and highly complex. This paper aims to introduce a KHO-KHO optimization (KKO) method, to optimize the coordination of DOCRs. The algorithm proposed in this study has been tested on the lEC microgrid test systems. The results indicate the efficacy of the proposed KKO algorithm in reducing the operating time of relays for optimal coordination of the DOCRs. The results obtained from the KKO algorithm are compared with those from other optimization algorithms. The current approach provides the lowest relay operating time with optimized TDS and PS. The analysis of the results shows that the KKO method is efficient, straightforward, and accurate.

articleTitle: Robust Control of DC-DC Buck Converter in DC Microgrid with CPL
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: DC-DC converters are broadly used in many industries, like electric vehicles, industrial inverters, telecommunications systems, and many others. However, these converters face many challenges when it comes to their performance, particularly when they are used with constant power load (CPL) which has negative-incremental resistance. These loads might lead to instability issues with the converter's output voltage. This manuscript offers a way out to the above stated challenge, a robust nonlinear control approach has been developed. The control strategy is constructed on passivity-based controller (PBC) and employs a nonlinear-disturbance observer (NDO) to increase controller effectiveness against CPL. The PBC ensures system stability by dissipating transient energy and on the other hand, NDO operates in parallel to compensate for disruptions via a feed-forward channel. This method produces high signal stability and quick recovery performance during load disturbances and uncertainties. The offered strategy to control has been evaluated through simulations using a MATLAB-SIMULINK model. The results showed that this strategy may effectively address instability issues created by CPL.

articleTitle: Design of Fuzzy-PID Controller Using Optimization Technique based Reduced Order Modelling
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: The design of a fuzzy-PID controller for Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Greywolf Optimization (GWO) approaches is explored in this study. With these techniques, we can convert a higher order system into a lower order model. Higher order physical systems are typically too difficult to analyze, enabling the replacement of the higher order system(HOS) with a lower order model that has less complexity while keeping the original system essential characteristics. The original system is typically improved using reduce order modelling (ROM), which lowers the complexity of the controller design by reducing the number of control parameters. The simulation outcomes using different optimization techniques for ROM, including PSO and GWO, are then contrasted with those obtained using more conventional ROM techniques, such as Pole Clustering, Pade Approximation, and Routh Approximation. The development of a controller for the reduced model that can also be implemented to the initial HOS is the next step. Here, the gain settings of a PID controller are chosen using a fuzzy logic-based control technique.

articleTitle: Solar Photovoltaic Grid's Protection Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Since the advent of economics, environmental alterations have begun to affect people's lives and natural activities, including climate change. The consumption of fossil fuels has risen since they were discovered, which is assumed to be the reason for this. Fossil fuels are predicted to be used for more than 15 billion metric tonnes of transportation, power, and other purposes per year, releasing dangerous gases that are harmful to human health. Resulting a good heed towards viable energy sources like wind and solar. Solar energy is becoming increasingly common because it is more trustworthy than wind energy. The growth of solar systems has made security precautions more important than ever. A variety of system components, including as the reliability of the photovoltaic panels one another, storage devices, and loads, must be taken into consideration by these safeguards. in order to improve redundancy. With the help of MATLAB, this article proposes a effective practical defence for solar power systems operating in island mode. The results are examined and summarized at the end.

articleTitle: Effect of Ageing and Moisture on Dielectric Properties of Natural Ester Impregnated Pressboard Insulation
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Natural Ester is a promising liquid dielectric for power transformer applications. It has good dielectric properties and it is fully bio-degradable. However, the degradation of natural ester-based paper insulation needs to be studied in detail for understanding the consequences of long-term operation with natural ester-based power transformers. This paper presents the study of the degradation of natural ester-based pressboard insulation under the influence of thermal ageing and moisture is studied through dielectric response measurements, i.e., Frequency domain Spectroscopy (FDS) and Polarization-Depolarization Current (PDC) measurements. It was observed that both thermal ageing and moisture contribute to rapid decline into the resistivity of the insulation as well as increase in dielectric losses.

articleTitle: Optimal Energy Management Methods of Electric Vehicle with Battery and Super-Capacitor
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)

authors.preferredName: D. V. Siva Krishna Rao K

abstract: The study of Electric Vehicles(EV) with battery Supercapacitor is considered to address the shortage of power density of energy storage system. For use of two Energy storage system(ESS) where energy management is carried out using Hybrid Energy Storage System(HESS). In this project, the best management strategy is proposed, using Pontryagin's stationery Principle which distributes the driving force at lightning speed while two ESS drive the vehicle immediately and Energy from regenerative braking is divided between the two ESSs. This work includes details on lithiumion batteries and supercapacitor hybrid energy storage systems for EVs. Results from the simulation are obtained and evaluated on a small scale while connected to a bidirectional DC-DC converter. Depending on the battery capacity, batteries can provide a longer electrical range, but they are less effective when utilized under high load conditions, leading to higher thermal stress and shorter battery life. Simulink/MATLAB is used to run the simulation. It features three modes of operation, including brushless DC motor propulsion for electric vehicle propulsion, with energy management and storage in between.

articleTitle: Wind Resource Assessment using MERRA-2 and Meteorological Mast Data
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: The most crucial factors in wind farm development are the best turbine selection, data collection accuracy, wind turbine positioning, and wake effect considerations. This work deals with the wind resource assessment (WRA) of an onshore wind farm with MERRA-2 Reanalysis data for repowering. The analysis is carried out by a comparison of Wind Resource Assessment (WRA) conducted through MERRA-2 Reanalysis data and meteorological data for investigating the variance through the comparison of MERRA- 2 and meteorological data, though the former is cheaper. The simulation is done using Wind Atlas Analysis and Application Program (WA<tex>$s$</tex>P) software by Denmark Technological University (DTU), and the major results obtained from WA<tex>$s$</tex>P after the wind farm modelling are Annual Energy Production (AEP), Wind Power Density (WPD), and Resource Grid.

articleTitle: Optimal Distributed Energy Resources Sizing for Behind-the-Meter Applications in Presence of Electric Vehicle Charging Load
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Increasing penetration of electric vehicle (EV) charging load presents challenges in optimally sizing microgrid distributed energy resources (DER) for performing behind the meter applications. This paper proposes a method to generate the most likely EV charging load profile for a site considering the number of chargers planned to be installed, their ratings, EV battery size and on/off-board charger rating and progressively estimating the state of charge of EV battery at the time of charging start. This paper also proposes a method to size DERs for optimally performing behind-the-meter applications in a microgrid considering the generated EV charging load profile, the EV charging cost, capability of managed charging of EV loads if needed and the uncertainties of charging start time. The method is demonstrated through a test case of sizing battery energy storage system for performing behind the meter applications for an industrial facility located in the city of Irvine, USA.

articleTitle: Active Voltage and Active Power Control of Doubly Fed Induction Generator by Using Novel Optimal Control of Current Source Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: The extraction of optimal power from wind energy-based doubly fed induction generators (DFIG) is an emerging area of research. Long-distance transmission systems are frequently connected with large-scale wind farms. The critical point voltage of a DFIG has a stability issue because of the change in wind speed. The capabilities of reactive power in the wind farm have been analyzed and the reactive power requirement of the system to keep constant access point voltage regardless of the variation in wind speed using a decoupled programmable control circuit has been done. For the DFIG wind energy conversion system (WECS), a unique current source converter (CSC) control technique is suggested. Although most studies on wind energy systems use voltage source converters, the shortcomings of conventional CSCs, such as large passive devices, low switching frequency, and slow dynamic performance, can be overcome with the advancement of semiconductor technology and reverse block insulated gate bipolar transistor (RB-IGBT) devices with high switching frequencies. WECS based on CSCs also has a number of benefits, including resilience, built-in fault ride-through capabilities, short-circuit protection, and more.

articleTitle: Application of Expected Sarsa-Learning for Load Frequency Control of Multi-Area Power System
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: This paper presents expected sarsa-Iearning algorithm-based control strategy for load frequency control of two-area power system. This algorithm comes under value- teration-based model-free reinforcement learning algorithm. The pre-learning for this algorithm is carried out on two area power system. Then the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy is evaluated on the modified two-area power system. DFIG-based wind power generation is incorporated into each area of the modified power system. The simulation study is demonstrated to analyse the performance of the proposed controller.

articleTitle: Electricity Price Forecasting in Markets Considering Renewable and EV penetration using Machine Learning and DNN
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: The deregulation of the energy market increased rivalry, compelling many strategy creators to choose forecasting electricity prices because the more accurate the projection, the better the strategy they can devise. In this work, we have utilized both the renewable energy source (RES) generation data and Electric Vehicle (EVs) energy demand data along with the historical electricity price (EP) data to analyze and evaluate the impact of the integration of EV and RES on the Electricity Price Forecasting (EPF), for the forecasting purpose we used various machine learning (ML) models and DNN models out of which we got the best results from the Random Forest of 1.98 mean absolute error (MAE),0.686 percent of mean absolute percentage error (MAPE), 2.12 root mean square error (RMSE) and 0.864 of r2 score, these results are further compared with the past result, and it can be analyzed that addition of EV demand data helps in improvement in the forecasting accuracy.

articleTitle: Technical-Economic-Environmental (TE2) analysis of different site suitability classes in India
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: India is currently confronted with the issues of fossil fuel import, greenhouse gas emissions, foreign dependence, energy security, and economic hardship. Thus, India must create a substantial amount of its own renewable and sustainable energy. However, the success of renewable energy projects, particularly solar energy projects, depends on the site selection. Site selection is a vital, multi-step procedure in the installation of a solar power plant since it has a direct impact on the plant's performance and economic viability. Therefore, the present article focuses on the site selection and techno-economic feasibility of a solar power plant at the selected site. The present study analyzed the geographical site suitability map of India, which includes the five classes of extremely favorable, favorable, moderately favorable, less favorable, and unfavorable. For each of the land suitability classes, the present study performed the technical-economic-environmental (TE2) analysis using the RETScreen software. The TE2 modelling outcome highlights that the extremely favorable land suitability class performed better in terms of the highest electricity exported to the grid (179440 MWh/year), least levelized cost of electricity (35.40 $/MWh), and maximum greenhouse gas emission reduction (153572-ton CO<inf>2</inf> per year). The order was followed by favorable, moderately favorable, and less favorable suitability sites.

articleTitle: Motors used for the development of Solar Pumping System: A Systematic Review
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: In present times, competition is going on among the pump industries to deliver an efficient pump that could have an extended life. For survival in this competitive market, the pump industry has been investing in research for producing better quality pumps at a reasonable price. To meet this challenge, the companies have now focussed on research on Permanent Magnet Motors in place of conventional induction motors for performance improvement of pumps. This paper presents a systematic review of the research done in designing the motors. Various papers were studied for the development of motors for solar submersible pumping. This systematic analysis has been presented to help the researchers for finding the performance gaps in the present borewell motors and future research scope in this area.

articleTitle: Lung Cancer Stage Prediction Using Multi-Layer Perceptron and Deep Learning Classifier
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Providing accurate diagnosis for cancer is a challenging problem in precision oncology. Multiomics Data about cancer cells comprises of details about cancer cells like their radius, texture, perimeter, area, smoothness, compactness, and concavity. Analysis of this data is very much useful in the prediction of the stage of cancer in Lung cancer patients. This project aims at analyzing the lung cancer cell data set and making a prediction for the given data using ada boost classifier and multi-layer perceptron deep learning classifier.

articleTitle: Uncertainty Management in Utility Grid Considering PV Generation: An Operational Planner's Perspective
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: This paper discusses the importance of adopting a spatiotemporal model-based scenario generation technique by approximating a multivariate continuous stochastic process in a discrete form. The computational steps for such a model development are comprehensibly discussed via a case study using PV generation data collected from the USA. The model accuracy comparison through a detailed discussion of obtained results is likely to help novice researchers to choose the best model amongst the available options and tactically decide to improvise the modeling framework further. This systematically prepared paper is expected to help power engineers with enough confidence to execute operational planning decisions realistically.

articleTitle: Rooftop Solar PV Assisted E-Rickshaw with Hybrid Energy Storage System
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: E-rickshaws (or Electric-rickshaw) have sparked a great deal of interest as a green and sustainable transit option, as compared to traditional auto rickshaws that use fossil fuels. The primary component that affects E-rickshaw mobility over the course of its lifetime is its Energy Storage System (ESS). In contemporary E-rickshaws, lead-acid batteries are the most common form of ESS, hence it's essential to prolong their lifespan. From this perspective, we assess the potential for updating the traditional E-rickshaw's energy generation and storage systems for technological and financial gain by employing a solar PV panel on the rooftop. Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) is generally selected, but it reacts slowly to unpredictable transient events. Therefore, to construct a Hybrid Energy Storage System (HESS), a high-power density ESS like a supercapacitor (SCs) must be combined with a battery. In this paper, a combination of solar PV panel is installed over the E-rickshaw roof, along with the combination of both battery and SC as HESS. It is observed that HESS provides average power over extended periods of time and manages transient situations optimally. It normalizes the voltage and power at the DC link and regulates it according to the IEC 61000-3-2 standard. Finally, the MATLAB Simulink framework is used for performance analysis of the proposed system.

articleTitle: Comparative Studies of Grid-Connected SEIG-Based WECS Using a Different Type of Control Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Paper presents the comparative studies between indirect vector control (IVC) based Grid-connected SEIG-based Wind Energy Conversion Systems (GCSEIGWECS) and Direct torque control (DTC) with Space Vector Pulse width Modulation (SVPWM) based GCSEIGWECS. The frequency converter includes a Rotor side Connected converter (RSCC) and Grid Side Connected Converter (GSCC) is used to control torque ripples, rotor speed overshoot, undershoot, active power, reactive power, and DC-Link Voltage. The Sinusoidal Pulse Width Modulation (SPWM) technique for RSCC and Space Vector Pulse width Modulation (SVPWM) for GSCC have been proposed. The different topologies have been implemented using MATLAB/SIMULINK tools.

articleTitle: On-board Converter for Electric Vehicle Charging using LCLC Resonant Topology
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Due to their high efficiency, high power density, and soft switching characteristics, LLC-based AC-DC resonant converters are a great choice for EV chargers. Adding a capacitor across the magnetizing inductance of the LLC resonant architecture (LCLC configuration) enhances efficiency and reduces the need for a larger series inductor. The output DC voltage of the converter is generally regulated using switching frequency control. However, the power factor of the converter varies significantly with the switching frequency. As a result, any fluctuations in load may cause the converter to operate at a lower power factor. This paper proposes a single-stage topology based on the LCLC resonant structure. Zero voltage switching (ZVS) of the IGBTs used in the converter is ensured by the LCLC resonant configuration. Converter have a power factor correction (PFC) stage on the front of the converter to achieve natural power factor correction. Since the PFC stage and the resonant stage are controlled by the same switches, the converter is smaller and less costly. Simulations in MATLAB/Simulink are used to validate the topology.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Current Control based Three-Level Inverter fed Five Phase Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Drive
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Industrial standards of torque control techniques like Direct Torque Control (DTC) and Field Oriented Control (FOC) are complex and do not achieve precise torque control, this work presents the implementation of Model Predictive Current Control (MPCC) for a Three-Level Inverter (3LI) fed Five Phase Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (PMSM) Drive. The objective is to minimize the torque ripple and reduce complexity using MPCC technique for the Three-level Inverter (3LI). This paper includes steady state and transient analysis under sudden load changes, speed reversal, step change of speed, and load variations. In order to show effectiveness of MPCC based 3LI fed PMSM it is compared with 2LI fed PMSM drive. A mathematical model of MPPC is presented and simulated, and the operational behavior of the MPCC-based 3LI fed Five Phase PMSM drive is evaluated using MATLAB/SIMULINK simulation platform.

articleTitle: Reliability Planning for $2\mathrm{x}25$ kV Traction Power Supply System: Fault Severity and Contingency Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: The involvement of autotransformers in a <tex>$2\mathrm{x}25 \mathbf{kV}$</tex> traction system increases the severity of faults. Unattended faults lead to component failure, making reliability planning essential for the system. This paper proposes a method of estimating the fault current variation with fault location using a node-admittance matrix-based approach. The system is further analyzed during various contingencies to ensure a robust design, and its performance is enhanced using Static Var Compensators (SVCs), An optimal voltage compensation algorithm is proposed to trigger in the event of any outage. A comparative analysis is presented on a 30 km sample feeding section, with SVCs placed at the substation and then at the sectioning post.

articleTitle: Investigation For Resource Exploitation of Solar Energy on The Roof of Pupils Houses- A Survey
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Solar energy is one of the important traditional energy supplements that help in creating a green energy balance sheet. Education system is the one which imparts value added education to the pupil. The nature's enrichment and its sustainability requirement can be achieved through motivation of the later. It is realized that there is sufficient space on the roof of pupils house, that at least a considerable capacity of solar PV system can be installed such that to the extent possible a part of their house hold electricity demand can be met and also excess generation can be pumped to the grid. In this paper a survey has been performed considering a pupil's strength about 179 members. The vacant net roof area and the daily electricity consumption of their houses has been evaluated and found that 10555.56 Sqm of vacant roof area can be allotted for erecting the solar PV system and about 1638.04 kWp capacity of solar PV plant can be erected within the identified area contributing 6552.18 kWh of electricity generation per day. This could meet 22.36 % of average concern household electricity demand and out of which 77.63% can be fed to the grid and in total leading to the reduction of 5569.35 kg of CO2 emissions per day.

articleTitle: Credible System for Industrial IoT Networks Using Block Chain Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: The industrial Internet of things specifies the interconnected network of instruments, sensors, and devices used in industrial applications, such as manufacturing and energy management. One technology that has the potential to improve IIoT systems is block chain, which can provide redundancy, immutable storage, and encryption. Another way to enhance IIoT security is to use data science techniques to detect and prevent malicious activities. This study aims to address the problem of malicious devices in industrial settings that can degrade network performance and compromise the security of legitimate IoT devices. To establish trust between IoT devices and safeguard the network from malicious entities, the coordinator's IoT device is used. While some open-source ciphers may still be vulnerable to attack, organizations can benefit from the scrutiny of numerous users, making it difficult for centralized entities or third parties to make malicious modifications. Additionally, integrating a block chain-based data model can ensure data transparency. The proposed framework is experimentally evaluated using MATLAB to measure a variety of security metrics such as the likelihood of false authentication, message tampering, and attack intensity. Based on the simulation results, it is observed that the suggested approach effectively improves the security of industrial IoT networks by identifying and mitigating malicious attacks.

articleTitle: Review of 3.3kW Electric Vehicle Charger
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: The development of electric vehicle technology has made batteries and their charging systems more susceptible to shift (EVs). To maintain and extend battery life, an extremely effective charger must be built. Two components make up the generalized charger: a DC-DC conversion stage with isolation and power factor correction, which is necessary to keep power factor near to unity. This paper compares various power factor correction circuits and dc/dc converter topologies in terms of technology, taking into consideration variables like cost, number of components, utilization power level, efficiency, and control complexity. For the 3.3kW on-board charger, an overview of charger types and selection is studied.

articleTitle: MIMO DC-DC Converter-based Photovoltaic Water Pumping System
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Globally the problem of diesel prices increasing substantially and the undersupply of electricity due to technicalreasons are major concerns for a water pumping system. If lookover India, diesel supply and price are affected by variousnational and international causes, but the shortage of electricity is linked to coal supplies and lack of funds in DISCOMs. The photovoltaic-based water pumping system (PVWPS) is a viable solution because it is essential to daily requirements and agricultural activities. However, because it uses less installed PV capacity than necessary, such PVWPS have a low return on investment. In order to solve this issue, a multi-input multi-output (MIMO) converter for PVWPS is suggested in this work. These features are included in the proposed MIMO converter: (i) multi-level voltage at multi-output terminals enables connection of diverse types of loads like three-phase AC load, single-phase AC load, and DC loads; (ii) capability to integrate multiple PV inputs and thus minimizing the power loss due to mismatching issues. A model of the MIMO-based PVWPS has been validated through MATLAB simulation and a satisfactory performance has been observed.

articleTitle: Assessing Seasonal Variations in CEP for NavIC Positioning in Dehradun Region
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: In this study, the seasonal variations of the Circular Error Probable (CEP) using the Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System (IRNSS) or NavIC system in the low latitude northern region of India during four seasons: summer, winter, spring, and autumn has been analyzed. The study used the data obtained from a dual-frequency IRNSS/GPS/SBAS (IGS) receiver installed at the Graphic Era University. The results showed that the CEP values varied significantly during different seasons. The analysis revealed that the highest CEP values were observed during the summer season, followed by the autumn season, while the lowest CEP values were observed during the winter season, followed by the spring season. This study provides valuable insights into the seasonal variations of CEP in the NavIC system, which can be useful in the design and implementation of various applications, such as precision agriculture and navigation systems for aerial vehicles. The results also highlight the need for further research to investigate the factors influencing the seasonal variations in CEP and to develop more accurate models for improved performance of the NavIC system. This study offers important insights on how NavIC signals vary in different seasons at a low latitude northern region of India.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Analysis of Electro Optic ToR(EO-ToR) for Low Latency Data Center Network
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Since last couple of decades, modern high-performance data center network (DCN) is liable for transporting most emerging cloud-centric application like big data, IoT, etc. to end users. To cope with the demand, futuristic DCN must be scalable, flexible, and reconfigurable with high bandwidth, low latency, less power requirement and less cabling complexity. Integration of electric packet switching and optical circuit switching is now an evolving research area in DCN architecture to get the best features of faster forwarding in packet switching and high bandwidth support in circuit switching. In DCN top of rack (ToR) switch acts as a bridge between servers and external switching circuit. To support packet switching and circuit switching parallel ToR is need to be designed in such a way, so that it can classify the packets as per the respective switching domains. In this paper we have proposed and modelled an Electro-Optic ToR (EO-ToR) that will classify the data compatible for packet switching and circuit switching domains respectively. To reduce the repetitive, look up and update of flow table of EO-ToR, M/MI1 queue with feedback is used to model the EO-ToR. The performance is measured in terms of latency and sojourn time in MATLAB platform and is compared with the traditional ToR. Observation of 18%-46% improved latency while 12%-35% decrement in sojourn time ensures the scalability and performance of integrated futuristic DCN architecture.

articleTitle: Harmonic Estimation of Modern Power System Using Improved Grey Wolf Optimization- Based Recursive Least Square Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: The integration of inverter interfaced distributed generations (IIDGs) in conventional power system greatly affect the power quality in terms of harmonics modulation. Hence accurate estimation of power system harmonics is highly desired to design proper filters for harmonics mitigation. This article presents a hybrid optimized technique combining improved grey wolf optimization (IGWO) and recursive least square (RLS) to estimate harmonics. The IGWO used for predicting the phase and RLS is used for determining amplitude of the signal. The performance of the proposed IGWO-RLS is tested using standard testing module. MATLAB/SIMULINK is used for signal generation and estimation. The efficacy of proposed estimation technique is verified in presence of noise and comparing with other hybrid estimation algorithm.

articleTitle: Privacy-Preserving and Verifiable Decentralized Federated Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Federated learning is a machine learning technique that allows multiple devices to collaboratively train a machine learning model without sharing their data with a central server. The data is kept on the local device, and the model is trained on the device itself. It also reduces the risk of data breaches and enhances privacy by keeping the data local to the device. It can improve the speed and efficiency of training large-scale models by distributing the workload across multiple devices. This paper proposes a solution to the security challenges faced by the federated learning framework, which allows global model construction without sharing raw data. Privacy-preserving and verifiable decentralized federated learning (PPVD-FL) is a framework designed for secure deep learning model training. It's a decentralized federated learning framework that pre-serves privacy and ensures verification. The framework uses an efficient and verifiable cipher-based matrix multiplication algorithm along with a suite of decentralized algorithms. It maintains the confidentiality of the global model and local updates and verifies every training step. PPVD-FL can protect privacy against various inference attacks and ensure training integrity, as shown by security analysis. Real-world experiments on datasets demonstrate its accuracy and practical performance.

articleTitle: A Reduced Switching Two-Vector MMPC Scheme for MMCs in Medium Voltage Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: A two-vector Modulated Model Predictive Control (MMPC) scheme is proposed in this paper that achieves reduced switching in the output pole voltage of a Modular Multilevel Converter (MMC). This switching state change reduction is significant when compared to the conventional three-vector pulse width modulation (PWM) scheme. The proposed two-vector scheme is generalized for any n-level pole voltage operation and is suitable for digital implementation. The three main control parameters in MMC i.e. output current, inner circulating current and submodule capacitor voltages are satisfactorily controlled while a reduced switching two-vector scheme is applied. The simulation results considering 10 submodules in each arm of 3-⊘MMC are showcased while feeding power to the medium voltage grid at unity power factor. Hardware results along with transient performance are also incorporated.

articleTitle: Study on Weakening the Effect of Air Density Changes for Increased Power Capture of Individual Wind Energy Conversion System
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: This article investigated the effect of weather parameter variations, such as air density and temperature changes, on the power capture of permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG)-based wind energy conversion systems (WECS). The air density of the area where the wind turbines are installed is continuously varied throughout the year. It can affect annual energy production because aerodynamic power is linearly dependent on the air density of the environment. In areas with high wind, this air density variation does not affect the power production of the WT much since the high wind can produce enough force to rotate the turbine blades. However, this effect results in a considerable power reduction in areas with low wind speeds. For this reason, it is important to develop a method that can reduce this variation in air density for increased power production. In order to weaken the effect, the appropriate readjustments of optimal blade position (or pitch angle) and optimal rotational speed will be made according to the weather condition data. The simulation study was conducted by using 2WM PMSG-based WECS in Matlab/Simulink®, and it revealed that the readjustment was effective in mitigating the effect of air density variations, and the power production of the WT was increased.

articleTitle: Spearman Correlation Coefficient Assisted Novel Methodology For Line Outage Identification Using PMU data
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Fast and accurate transmission line outage identification (TLOI) is very much needed to maintain the reliability and security of the power system. A single line outage will result into the outage of another line and cascading failure may propagate into complete or partial system blackout. In this context, a novel mathematical model is developed in this paper using synchronized measurements of the phasor measurement unit (PMU) for transmission line outage identification (TLOI). A new logical term, namely cost function value (CFV) is defined using the concept of Spearman correlation coefficient (SCC). The TLOI problem is solved through the proposed CFV by comparing the simulated line powers (SLPs) for several LOCs with measured line powers (MLPs) obtained from PMUs. Furthermore, the uncertainty of measurement is also included in the developed mathematical model via random Gaussian noise vector. The developed model is applied on benchmark IEEE 6,14,57 bus networks in the MATLAB environment. Comparative evaluation of the proposed methodology with some existing methods is also carried out to corroborate the effectiveness and applicability of developed model.
