articleTitle: Designing a Control Strategy for PV-Wind-BESS based Microgrid system and Integrating it with a Weak Grid
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Policy makers and researchers are looking towards renewable energy sources due to the rising realization in emissions of greenhouse gases and the implications of these pollutants, as well as the ever-increasing need for electric energy. These renewable energy sources are connected in a distributed manner along with the loads constituting microgrids (MG). As a consequence of this, MG that utilise a variety of sources of energy have made significant strides in the past several years, paving the way for the integration of hybrid MG with the power systems that are already in place. However, it is required to conduct an in-depth critical analysis of the practical challenges involved in the control strategy of these MG. In this context, this paper will discuss a control strategies like voltage control, current control and frequency control of micro sources in MG along with droop based MG voltage controller. Islanding of MG is investigated in both the cases when MG imports the power from grid and exports the power to the weak grid. The overall model is simulated and the performance of the proposed controller is investigated by considering solar photovoltaic (PV), wind energy and battery energy storage system (BESS) based MG integrated to the grid. Performance analysis has been carried out to verify how well the proposed controller works.

articleTitle: Design of Three-port Isolated Bidirectional Efficient EV Charging System with DPS Control
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: This paper presents an isolated three-port bidirectional charging system for electric vehicle (EV). This includes a power-factor correction (PFC) rectifier, a series resonant converter (SRC), and a blocking capacitor-based dual- active bridge (DAB) converter. The SRC is intended for fast charging, while the DAB converter is intended for slow charging. The three-port converter (TPC) reduces the number of components which ultimately minimizes the cost and volume of the converter. To manage the power flow of different ports, a dual-phase shift (DSP) control approach with frequency modulation has been implemented. In this work, SRC has been tested to obtain an output voltage of 200 V, while DAB has been tested for 50 V output. The simulation study has been carried out in MATLAB/Simulink environment.

articleTitle: Investigating the Effect of Weather Conditions on the Performance of a Modified Solar Cooker with Inclined Outer Cover
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Solar cookers use the sun's radiation energy to cook food, providing an alternative to traditional cooking methods. Box-type solar cookers are simple to construct and operate, making them a popular choice for use in rural areas and developing countries. However, the performance of a box-type solar cooker may vary depending on the prevailing weather conditions, which may affect the amount of solar energy received and the cooking temperature achieved. This research paper aims to investigate the effect of weather conditions on the performance of a Modified solar cooker with inclined outer cover (MSCIOC). The study involved conducting experiments under different weather conditions, including sunny, partly cloudy, and overcast days, to determine the impact of these conditions on the cooking temperature achieved and the cooking time. The figure of merits obtained (<tex>$\mathbf{F}_{\mathbf{1}}$</tex> & <tex>$\mathbf{F}_{\mathbf{2}}$</tex>) are 0.113 and 0.41, cooking power is 86 W, cooking time is 252 minute and theoretical cooking time is 233 minutes. The results of this study will provide insights into the optimal conditions for using a box-type solar cooker and inform the development of strategies for improving their performance.

articleTitle: Modified Decomposition Method for Complex Bridge Network
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Belief reliability is a new reliability metric that accounts for aleatory uncertainty and epistemic uncertainty. Belief reliability is based on the uncertainty theory it considers epistemic and aleatory uncertainty. Finding the distribution of belief dependability depending on the real conditions is crucial to understanding belief reliability, but doing so can be challenging when there is a lack of knowledge availability of components. The issue of belief reliability of systems has been addressed recently. These methods of Belief reliability are inefficient in the process of deriving system reliability expression as these methods generate both cancelling and non-cancelling terms. Also the number of terms in the expression of Belief Reliability are large enough. To resolve these issues an efficient method is proposed that considers a priori knowledge of minimal paths and cuts of the system. The method generates only success terms (non-cancelling terms) and number of terms in Belief Reliability expression are very less as compared to existing method. The findings are quantified and the results are validated with the help of Benchmark problem i.e. Bridge Network.

articleTitle: Optimized Multi-model Machine Learning Approach for Residential Load Prediction
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Accurate prediction of the residential load is important to increase the utilization of available local energy resources, to address over/under voltage problems, and overloading issues in low voltage (LV) distribution grids. The need for an optimized prediction model has been observed that performs well even when the dataset has characteristic deviations. This paper aims to present an optimized model for residential electrical load prediction. Linear regression, regression tree, ensemble, and gaussian process regression (GPR) methods are considered, and based on the error metrics evaluation, a prediction model with minimum error is selected for load prediction. Calendar and weather-based features are selected based on the principal component analysis. A case study has been performed, considering the measured smart meter data from a multi-storied residential house in Houston, Texas, USA. A comparison of predicted and measured residential electrical load shows that the suggested approach performs satisfactorily.

articleTitle: Load frequency control of two area power systems using optimised ANFIS controller
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: In this paper, novel, innovative Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference Systems (ANFIS) have been designed for the application of Load Frequency Control (LFC) in a nonlinear Two Area Power System (TAPS) consisting of a non-reheat thermal plant as a single source. Firstly, the training and testing data of the ANFIS controller is obtained by tuning the TAPS using Honey Badger Algorithm (HBA) for each area. Then this data is used to train two ANFIS controllers by taking Area Control Error (ACE) and derivative of ACE as inputs. Finally, the time response analysis is performed for the system's frequency deviation and tie-line power change. The critical parameters such as Settling Time, Peak Undershoot, Peak Overshoot, and Integral of Time-weighted Absolute Error (ITAE) are studied under 5% of load disturbance of the two-area power system. The obtained results show the better performance of the proposed ANFIS controllers compared to HBA and other existing controllers available in the literature for the FLC of the two-area power system.

articleTitle: Numerical Investigation of the Performance Characteristics in a Radial Disc Micro-Combustor for Various Geometrical and Operating Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: The present study is a numerical investigation on the Hydrogen-air premixed combustion in a micro disc- radial burner with an annular step of curved profile. Micro disc-radial burner with a curved-in annular step with diameters of 0.5mm., 0.625mm and 0.75mm are considered in this study. Average combustion efficiency and upper wall temperature are used as metric to quantify the combustion and heat transfer performance of the micro-burner. The average combustion efficiency in the micro-disc burner is observed to monotonously decrease with increase in inlet velocity. The results show that the effect of the inlet velocity on the average upper wall temperature is non-monotonous. The average upper wall temperature decreases with the initial increase in the inlet velocity to reach a minimum. However, further increase in the inlet velocity is observed to increase the average upper wall temperature for all the curved-in step burners. Also, the increase in the inlet velocity is noticed to result in the micro-disc burner to exhibit more uniform upper wall temperature. The curved-in step is observed to result in a significant drop in the outer-wall temperature compared to the burner with a conventional step. An increase in the diameter of the curvature is observed to cause a further drop in the average upper wall temperature. The average combustion efficiency is also noticed to decrease for the curved-in step burners. The adverse effect of the curved-in step on the combustion performance could be attributed to the downstream movement of the point of reattachment of the fluid separated at the step with the combustor wall.

articleTitle: Design of 3.6 GHz Rectenna with Broad Power Range for Efficient Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: In this paper, a rectenna (antenna + rectifier) is proposed for ambient RF energy harvesting. A modified rectangular microstrip patch antenna with inset feed is designed at 3.6 GHz with a gain of 4.3 dB. The antenna is compact in size with a layout area of <tex>$0.36\lambda \mathrm{x}\ 0.36\lambda$</tex> where <tex>$\lambda$</tex> is free space wavelength corresponding to resonating frequency. The antenna resonates at 3.6 GHz with impedance bandwidth (IBW) <tex>$(\mathbf{lS}_{11} < -20\ \mathbf{dB})$</tex> of 4.53% and a radiation efficiency of 68.5% is noted. To hoard the available RF energy, a simple RF-DC rectifier is designed using equal ripple Low Pass Filter (LPF) on FR4 substrate with height of 1.6mm. To improve the efficiency of the rectifier and to achieve broad range power conversion efficiency (PCE), additional radial stubs are incorporated on the rectifier design. Maximum PCE of 60.7 % is achieved with a load of <tex>$2\mathbf{K}\Omega$</tex> at 7dBm. The novelty of RF- DC rectifier is PCE of above 30% is achieved for broad range of input power (−10 dBm to 10 dBm).

articleTitle: A Generalized Scheme for Attaining Maximum Power Point Tracking and Voltage Regulation in PV Integrated System
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: In this paper a generalized scheme for attaining the two significant objectives in Photo-voltaic (PV) integrated system i.e., Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) and Voltage regulation has been proposed under different environmental and operating scenarios. A single converter- based control scheme has been proposed to extract maximum power under varying degree of solar irradiance and voltage regulation under dynamic loading conditions. The controller is tuned to execute the desired objective as per the requirement of the application. The scheme has been extensively validated for real time environment in terms of extracting maximum power during irradiance change and maintaining the desired voltage under varying load.

articleTitle: Performance Improvement of EV using K - Map Constructed Rule Based Energy Management Strategy for Battery / UC HESS
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: The performance improvement of Hybrid Energy Storage System (HESS) in Electric Vehicle (EV) has been in discussion over the last decade. The important issues in terms of performance parameters addressed are the range of the vehicle and battery (BA) peak current. This paper deals with both range improvement in EV and battery peak current reduction by applying a Karnaugh Map (K-Map) constructed rule-based energy management strategy to proposed HESS. The strategy allows Ultracapacitor (UC) to assist battery when the vehicle accelerates thereby reducing the burden on battery. Simulation is carried out for various operating modes of EV considering both urban and highway driving conditions. Simulation is done for different values of UC by keeping battery rating constant for each driving cycle and results are presented. The feasible value of UC is selected based on simulation results. The results of proposed HESS shows an improvement in performance parameters compared to Battery only Energy Storage System (BESS). Battery life is improved to a considerable extent and there is an overall development in the performance of electric vehicles.

articleTitle: Optimal Placement and Sizing of Custom Power Devices using PSO and APSO Optimization in Radial Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: In today's electricity system, power quality is a significant concern regardless of the voltage or current level. To address this issue, custom power devices (CPDs) have been introduced. In the considered system, six nonlinear load have been placed at different locations to introduce harmonics into the system. This paper focuses on strategic placement of CPDs in IEEE 15 bus system using MATLAB software. The primary objective is to minimize both the voltage total harmonic distortion (THD) and the individual harmonic distortion. The constraints ensure that the levels remain within the established standards, while also maintaining the voltage of each node within specified limits. Additionally, the study examines the performance of allocated CPD in controlling voltage quality and reactive power. In this work, particle swarm optimization (PSO) and adaptive particle swarm optimization (APSO) techniques have been employed to determine the optimal sizing and siting of CPDs. A comparison of the results obtained from these optimization methods is presented.

articleTitle: A Battery-Ultracapacitor Based Electric Vehicle with Regenarative Braking System
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: The need for an Alternative source of energy for automobiles has massively increased these days to reduce our dependence on fossil fuels because they have negative impact on the environment and also because they are fast depleting. The world is looking at electric vehicles as an alternative to fossil fuel-based automobiles as they are environment friendly in nature to an extent. Electric vehicles use conventional batteries to charge the motors which. The problem with the conventional batteries is that their performance degrades after multiple charging and discharging cycles whereas the issue with the other alternate storage options like supercapacitor is that it discharges very quickly. Hence, this paper aims to present an alternative hybrid EV model where the advantages of both the conventional batteries as well as the supercapacitors can be utilized in a way so as to enhance the overall working of the electric vehicle. The model also tries to incorporate the concept of regenerative breaking so as to utilize the heat energy generated during the breaking of the electric vehicle. Finally, the simulation results of this hybrid model is demonstrated.

articleTitle: A Novel Protection Coordination Scheme Based on Dual-Setting Rate of Change of Voltage Based Relays
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: An efficient and reliable relay coordination scheme is essential to protect the power system from faults and damages due to unexpected events such as short circuits. To cope with the reverse direction of fault current dual-setting relays are evolved. This paper presents a novel protection coordination scheme based on a dual-setting rate-of-change-of-voltage (DS-ROCOV) relay which remains unaffected during load and generation changes and is applicable to different network topologies. The DS-ROCOV relay offers two different settings each for primary and backup protection. It also ensures that the protection system is sensitive to high resistance faults. The performance of the proposed protection coordination scheme is evaluated by simulating various fault conditions in IEEE 9-bus system using MATLAB/Simulink. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed protection coordination scheme is effective in detecting and isolating faults while ensuring a quick response and minimizing unnecessary system outages. Overall, the proposed protection coordination scheme using DS-ROCOV enhances the reliability and selectivity of the protection systems in power distribution systems.

articleTitle: Fault Detection and Classification in Transmission Lines using Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Large interconnected electric power transmission lines are vital for delivery of continuous power flow to various loads. Due to this wide spread phenomena, transmission lines are more prone to electric faults and may lead to poor reliability of the power system. Thus, this paper tries to detect and classify various types of faults on interconnected transmission lines by utilizing artificial intelligence. A Back Propagation Neural Network (BPNN) is developed with three phase voltages/currents with zero sequence components. The performance of proposed BPNN based fault identification methodology is validated under various symmetrical and unsymmetrical faults on the IEEE 14- bus test power system. The simulation results reveal that the proposed fault identification methodology has accurately detected and classified all types of transmission line fault scenarios in the complex power system. Thus, the proposed artificial intelligence based fault identification concept can be quite suitable for protection of transmission lines in the electric grid.

articleTitle: Microcontroller Assist Fault Detection for Microgrids Based on Discrete Wavelet Transform
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Microgrids are small independent network of electricity which has its own sources of power generation. Microgrids work independently and can also take power from main grid. Most microgrids have inverter based distributed generations and energy storage System (ESS) which makes fault detection and isolation challenging for classical fault detection methods due to lower current contribution by distributed energy resources. Fault detection and isolation is the major challenge in operation of microgrids and essential for safe and reliable functioning of load connected. This paper proposes a novel approach for microgrid protection using discreet wavelet transform (DWT) which is a very efficient signal processing tool, this approach uses multiresolution analysis of three phase current signals by wavelet decomposition. The spectral entropy of the three-phase current signals are calculated in real time in a Microcontroller which gives the trip signal to circuit breaker by breaker control logic at different fault conditions. This system is verified as controller hardware in loop (CHIL) with a real-time digital simulator (RTDS) and microgrid model developed in RSCAD. Test and Simulation results shows that the proposed microgrid protection scheme is accurate and evades the problems faced by classical protection schemes in microgrid protection. This Protection scheme is easy to implement and does not require any complex or expensive equipment's.

articleTitle: Harmonic Analysis of Renewables and Electric Vehicle Penetrated Distribution System
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Due to the switching of any line, three-phase capacitor bank, nonlinear load unit, transformer, and Electric vehicle in a distribution system, harmonic components are generated in the measured signal. During the initiation of any high impedance fault (HIF) in the distribution system the presence of high frequency components in the range 2–20 kHz is significant. So, any protection algorithm based on total harmonic distortion (THD) percentage or harmonic components used for HIF detection may mal-operate during the above-mentioned dependable situations. In this paper, a detailed analytical report of different switching events is provided. The presence of different harmonic components during different switching events are highlighted and discussed.

articleTitle: Smart Door Keeper
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: With the advancements in computer vision, computers are now able to recognize and process various objects present in images. This technology has the potential to make life more convenient and improve society. Facial recognition is a task that computers perform better than humans, especially when searching through large databases of faces. In this paper, we present a system that uses computer vision to enhance home security. When someone presses the doorbell, the system detects the person in front of the door. If the person is recognized by the system, then the door can be unlocked. However, if the person is not known, the system will search for logos to identify the delivery company the person represents. If there are no logos detected, then the person is marked as an unknown guest, and the homeowner is notified. Our system includes a front-end, which allows the homeowner to add new people to the database, so on their next visit, the system can recognize them and send a notification accordingly. Additionally, we implemented algorithms for face recognition based on Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HOG) and object detection for identifying the lo-gos of different companies using Oriented FAST and Rotated BRIEF (ORB). This paper presents our system design, software algorithms, implementation, and results, along with a review of relevant work in the field of home automation systems. The traditional system only achieves alerting the home by the sound of a doorbell but nothing regarding identification, record keeping, and surveillance. The agenda is to create a smart doorbell system that incorporates the aspects of record keeping, home automation, and security.

Author Keywords: Histogram of Oriented Gradients(HOG) and ORB(Oriented FAST and Rotated BRIEF)

articleTitle: Model Predictive Control of Non-Minimum Phase DC-DC Boost Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: A perfect controller for DC-DC boost converter should be able to track the reference set point voltage that is higher than the source voltage along with minimum computational complexity. In this paper, a model predictive controller (MPC) is proposed for DC-DC boost converter control to regulate the output voltage under different operating conditions such as variation in input voltage and load current. The prediction is performed by the state space model and optimization is done using quadratic programming. The control performance of the converter is studied by varying prediction horizons with model disturbances. Finally, the hardware implementation of the proposed system is developed using dSPACE 1103 controller.

articleTitle: Probabilistic Modeling and Outage Analysis for Smart Microgrid and Electric Vehicles Ecosystem
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: In this work, we propose a simple yet novel prob-abilistic model for a renewable smart-grid and electric vehi-cle (EV) ecosystem supported by cellular vehicle-to-grid (C- V2G) infrastructure. Our stochastic model accounts for two key energy components modeled as random variables: the energy available from renewable sources and energy consumed by the EV. We define novel performance measures, desire probability, and threshold for the ratio of two energy components for this stochastic model. For it, we develop an insightful analysis that includes mathematical derivations for obtaining a single integral expression for the desired probability for a stable green grid- EV ecosystem operation. We present various numerical plots with varying model parameters and obtain useful insights to understand the model and suggest the optimum threshold for stable and safe operation. The model and analysis we develop are useful as the theoretical benchmark for other learning-based practical approaches.

articleTitle: Assessment of Power System Security using Contingency Ranking Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: With an ever-increasing demand for power in dif-ferent applications, the incorporation of various strategies for generating, transmitting and distributing power has become crucial in the current electric power system planning. In the midst of this, monitoring the security of the power system under contingencies (outage of line and generator) has also become very crucial, so that there will not be any uncertainty in the network, and there will be a continual supply of power to the load. This paper presents the security assessment of the power system under the N -1 contingency of both the line and generator unit. Contingency ranking is done to determine the severity of each contingency. In this paper, two approaches are employed for contingency ranking, using the AC power flow method and the Performance Index method. IEEE 57-bus system is employed for testing the proposed approaches using MATLAB. It has been observed that both approaches obtain nearly the same rankings, and Performance Index method is chosen to be the best method for the contingency analysis.

articleTitle: Energy Harvesting circuit for Digitization of Wiegand Pulse using Buck Converter in Discontinuous Conduction Mode
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Energy harvesting using Wiegand sensor as self-sustaining sensor is an emerging research area. The Wiegand sensor is a magnetic sensor that relies on the phenomenon of large Barkhausen jumps, generates a triangular voltage pulse upon the application of an alternating magnetic field. Pulse generation occurs regardless of how slowly the magnetic field variation occurs, is an attractive feature which enables its use as an energy harvester even in presence of low-frequency sources. Wiegand sensor as a sensing element have been used in many applications. But Wiegand sensor as energy harvester opens interesting, yet still overlooked possibilities in the energy harvesting field. The major challenge with the Wiegand sensor is energy harvested per pulse in the range of nJ. In this research work, we have proposed the circuit using Wiegand sensor that uses buck converter in discontinuous mode (DCM) mode to generate the digital pulse of 4.5 V and 10 ms at extremely low frequency for each magnetic field reversal without the use of any external power supply. Battery-less digital pulse generation is demonstrated for rotating application in the present study. The operating frequency up to 100 Hz has been considered. The main advantage of the proposed circuit is digitization of triangular shape Wiegand pulse is feasible for extremely slow varying magnetic field which can be used directly by microcontroller unit for further analysis.

articleTitle: Prosumer Driven Virtual Power Plant Profit Maximization Considering Demand Response
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: The Energy systems are changing Dramatically from downstream power delivery to smart distribution and bidirectional power flows, from top-down topologies to decentralized local structure. These changes break monopoly in power generation and enables energy democracy due to renewable based power generation and integration. A Virtual Power Plant (VPP) is an innovative approach to power generation and energy trading that connects multiple decentralized generation units, such as solar panels farm, wind turbines, and micro-turbines, through cloud-based software control systems. By aggregating and coordinating these units, a VPP acts as a flexible power plant that can respond to market demands and optimize operations in real-time. The primary purpose of a VPP is to participate in energy trading, specifically addressing uncertainties associated with Renewable Energy Sources (RESs), by balancing the intermittent nature of renewables and maximizing their utilization. To optimize electricity consumption, the paper proposes a conventional demand response approach called Time of Use (TOU). It divides the day into two time zones: the excessive zone (E-Zone) and the non-excessive zone (NE-Zone). Shifting electricity consumption between these zones based on pricing and demand patterns enables effective load scheduling. The research aims to demonstrate how the VPP can enhance its participation in the day-ahead energy market, ensuring cost-effective and reliable electricity supply. This work contributes to the development of advanced energy management strategies that promote renewable energy integration and facilitate a more sustainable and efficient energy future. The optimization is carried out in a General algebraic modeling system (GAMS) environment using CPLEX Solver. The VPP Profit is observed before and after the implementation of Demand Response.

articleTitle: A Demand and Response Management Model Using Load Forecasting Technique for Smart Grid
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Demand and response management plays a vital role in the smart grid for reliability between utility providers and smart meter customers. The demand of customers is predicted by load forecasting algorithms. However, existing load forecasting techniques consume high computation costs and limited forecasting accuracy. In this paper, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) is implemented for smart meter prediction of load. The proposed work is simulated on Open Energy Data Initiative (OEDI) dataset and our model outperforms the existing works in performance analysis. Mean Squared Error (MSE) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE) are achieved up to 0.0021 and 0.0332, respectively, by proposed model.

articleTitle: Soft Computing Technique for Automatic Detection, Classification and Location of Transmission Line Faults
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Proper monitoring and control of power system includes detection of Transmission lines faults. Faults in transmission line is the main factor in power interruption. To ensure a reliable, high quality, uninterrupted power supply to consumers, a smart, efficient, accurate system that can detect, classify, and locate faults is important. Artificial Neural Network (ANN) is one of the best choice for it. However, acquiring real fault data is difficult due to high data processing needs, security issues etc. Therefore, in this paper a transmission line is modelled using MATLAB/Simulink and dataset to train the neural network is generated by simulating the Simulink model for various fault types and different fault location. Three phase RMS voltages and currents measured on the sending end bus is input to the neural network to train it. Later the trained ANN model is tested by applying random unknown set of data. The simulation results exhibit good performance, ANN can effectively detect, classify and locate the faults.

articleTitle: Grid Following and Grid Forming Control Modes of DER Fed VSI with Transition of Operational Modes for Microgrid with Critical Load
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Quality and continuity of electrical power supplied to the consumers especially to the critical loads is very crucial irrespective of any kind of discrepancies in the power system. With the rigorous intervention in the domain of distribution energy resource (DER) and power electronics technology, there is a progressive growth of microgrid ecosystem in the power sector. However, this progressive approach catalyzes fluctuations in the service provided to the critical loads. Hence, the proposed work presents a control algorithm to operate a DER fed voltage source inverter (VSI) in grid following mode and grid forming mode under three different condition of microgrid operation while prioritizing critical load demand. Also, accurate transition of control modes of the VSI is taken care of by the presented controller while regulating the voltage and current requirements of the load. The proposed control strategy is then verified through simulation studies using MATLAB/Simulink under different operating conditions, such as grid-connected with and without DER, islanded, and transition between grid connected and islanded states. Further, the control approach has been experimentally examined to substantiate the proposed work.

articleTitle: Radar Communication via Asymmetric and Wideband Chaotic Signal
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: In this work, an asymmetric chaotic system with its circuit design and used for secure RADAR signal transmission. The chaotic system has four nonlinear terms, asymmetric behavior and wideband frequency spectra and large bandwidth. The chaotic signal/system is simulated in NI Multisim circuit design suite. The distinct and unique nature of chaotic signal can be utilized for RADAR communication to modulate the RADAR signal with the chaotic signal as a carrier signal. The chaotic modulation of the RADAR signal using the chaotic signal at the transmitter end via one the RADAR and demodulation is achieved at the receiver end via other RADAR and secure RADAR signal communication is accomplished. Numerical simulation is done in MATLAB and validated with achieved circuit simulation in NI Multisim which shows good agreement to that of MATLAB simulated results.

articleTitle: Outage and BER Analysis of Full Duplex Two Way Communication system using Multi IRS
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Anstract- The need for ultra speed, low latency and high reli-able communication between users is the demand throughout the world. This leads to utilize millimeter and Terahertz frequency band spectrum for efficient communication. The millimeter and Terahertz signal gets easily distorted by environment while using for long distance communication. A revolutionary technology called Intelligent Reflecting Surface (IRS) has the potential to completely transform the wireless communication sector by enabling high-speed, low-power, and reliable communication sys-tems. In this paper, a Full Duplex (FD) Two Way communication system using multi IRS is consider. While using single IRS there might not be Line of Sight (LoS) communication between the IRS and sources, Thus multi IRS is used for improve LoS communication and signal strength. A closed form expression for Outage Probability (OP) of the multi IRS system is derived. The monte carlo simulation validate the analytical expression. Further Bit Error Rate (BER) simulation for the proposed Full Duplex (FD) Two Way communication system is also analysed. The Signal to Noise Ratio (SNR) has been improved for both BER and OP while compared to single IRS assisted Two Way FD communication systems. Achievable rate for various location of IRS system in a Two Way FD communication systems is compared with single IRS system.

articleTitle: Survivability Assessment of a DG-enabled Power Distribution System through Network Reconfiguration
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: The topology of network reconfiguration is being widely used in electrical power distribution systems for many years now. This restructuring of the network provides an efficient solution to reduce the power loss and improve the overall voltage profile of the system significantly while requiring not much investment cost. This further improves the survivability of the power network. In this paper, a 10-bus power distribution network has been considered to analyze its survivability under several loading conditions. Distributed Generations (DGs) also play an important role to improve system survivability. This power grid survivability or resiliency with Distributed Generation (DG) included at specific buses has been also analyzed in this paper by evaluating a survivability index of the system. Lesser the survivability index, more will be the survivability of the system under any contingency (like fault, overloading etc.). The optimum network configuration with best survivability at a particular loading has been also determined here. A simulation load-flow is conducted in ETAP software for survivability assessment of a 10-bus power network.

articleTitle: Behaviour of Induced Currents in HVAC, EHVAC and UHVAC Lines During Short Circuits
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Increasing the capacity of the transmission line keeping power constant, the current flow in the line reduces thereby decreasing I<sup>2</sup>R losses, this in turn increases the efficiency of the transmission line. On the contrary, with the increase in transmission line voltage, a problem of electrostatic and electromagnetic coupling between the phases of the conductor and the conductive object surrounding the overhead transmission line is a major concern. Generally, the magnitude of coupling between the phases and between the line and the conducting object increases at high potential/voltage of transmission line during various fault scenarios. Thus, the behavior of induced currents and voltages i.e. coupling phenomena is studied at different voltage level of the transmission line i.e. HVAC, EHVAC and UHVAC under various short circuit events. The above simulation work is performed by using QuickField software. The simulation results reveal the impact of induced currents in high voltage transmission lines and the information is quite useful in design of bulk transmission lines of the electric grid.

articleTitle: Smart Traffic Detection and Control using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: In the modern era, with the rise in vehicles and population, many urban cities have faced traffic problems like traffic congestion, which causes travel delays. The main reason for the delay is that current traffic systems use fixed signal timers at the traffic signal intersection. These unnecessary delays at the traffic signals lead to excessive fuel consumption and increased pollution. This paper uses vehicle detection methods through surveillance cameras and machine learning to predict traffic based on historical data in a region. Finally, optimizing traffic by utilizing the predicted data and proposed methodology reduces the average wait time of travelers.

articleTitle: A method for Localization of Single source Partial Discharges using Acoustic Sensors and Random Forest Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Partial Discharge localization is of vital importance in the context of condition monitoring of power transform-ers and other High Voltage equipment. Acoustic sensors offer quite straightforward method for localizing PD sources in such insulation systems through measuring the time difference of arrival (TDOA) between signals captured at multiple acoustic sensors placed on the walls of the transformer tank. However, in such cases, simultaneous measurement across multiple sensors is required which increases the complexity as well as the cost of the overall PD detection system. In this work, an alternate scheme is proposed for localizing PD sources through application of Random Forest Algorithm, a well-known machine learning technique. An experimental set-up has been developed emulating a real-life transformer tank with PD sources present within it and three acoustic sensors were placed at three walls of the tank. The location of the PD was varied and corresponding to each location, the generated acoustic signals measured by each sensor at a time connected with an oscilloscope. Suitable features were extracted from this recorded data corresponding to each location. These features were used for training and testing of a random forest based machine learning model. From the testing results, it was observed that the developed model can locate single source PD with an accuracy of over 90 %.

articleTitle: New 4D Chaotic System with Infinite Equilibrium and Secure Colour Image Encryption
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: A new four-dimensional chaotic system is proposed here which has hidden attractors and infinitely many equilibrium points. The nature of the dynamics of the system is studied using bifurcation diagrams, phase portraits and Lyapunov exponent plots. The coexistence of fixed points surrounded by chaotic attractors is realized while fixing the variables and altering the initial values. An amplitude control is investigated for the proposed chaotic system. Concurrently a new algorithm for colour image encryption is developed using the proposed chaotic system. The potential of the algorithm against statistical and differential attacks is confirmed by some fundamental security analysis.

articleTitle: Rooftop Solar PV Socket Parity for Commercial Buildings in India
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Indian government has set a target of reducing emissions intensity by 33%-35% by 2030 of 2005 level and increasing the portfolio of non-fossil-based energy sources above 40% in the electricity mix by 2030. For this one of the steps initiated is the installation of 40 GW rooftop solar PV by 2022. The grid electricity tariff is increasing for consumers and in the last decade, it has escalated by five percent annually. From the consumer's standpoint, rooftop solar PV is viable when electricity is produced at a lower cost than grid electricity price, which is termed “Grid parity”. For examining the economic viability of 10 kWp and 50 kWp solar PV roof-mounted systems for buildings in India, 30 major cities of India were considered for the RETscreen simulation. The study found that 10 kWp and 50 kWp grid-connected rooftop solar PV is a viable alternative for the energy supplied by the grid for commercial buildings. The amount invested for the installation of 10 kWp and 50 kWp rooftops solar PV plants for commercial buildings in Indian cities can be recovered within 3 to 7 years. The study concluded that the 10 kWp and 50 kWp rooftops solar PV for commercial buildings have a widespread socket parity in Indian states.

articleTitle: Regulation Mileage-based Generation Command Dispatch
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: This paper constructs an optimal generation command dispatch scheme for automatic generation control (AGC) systems in a performance-based frequency regulation market. The approach incorporates the mileage-based strategy to dispatch correction signals among various AGC units while simultaneously minimizing power deviation and regulation mileage payment. The particle swarm optimization method has been adopted to obtain the optimal solution in the proposed AGC dispatch framework while considering the dynamic constraints. Finally, the effectiveness of this method has been tested on the single-area system and the extended two-area LFC system.

articleTitle: Slip Frequency Excitation for Variable Speed Wound-Field Synchronous Motor
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: This paper discusses a new wound field variable speed synchronous motor topology that has the exciter coupled to the same shaft as the main motor. The mechanism of excitation is similar to that of a brushless alternator, but since the motor has a varying speed, the relative speed of the exciter rotor flux with respect to its stator is kept constant. This is facilitated by having a slip frequency supply to the exciter stator. In order to validate field production, the main motor is supplied with a slow-ramping three-phase voltage, which causes the main rotor to lock with the field and run as a synchronous motor. The design of such a motor with a precise control mechanism reduces cost, enhances the overall speed-range, and ensures safe field shutdown in the event of loss of normal control, preventing overvoltage due to a fast spinning motor. Most of the currently used commercial motors employ permanent magnet rotors, but the availability of raw materials used for production of this particular subsystem is grossly inadequate in our country, resulting in large-scale imports of the same. As an effort towards import substitution, apart from the objective of enhancing operational efficiency, this study has made a beginning towards substituting permanent magnets with an electromagnet. In this context, this paper details the outcome of using slip frequency excitation coupled with scalar control on the performance of the motor.

articleTitle: Non-Contact Fault Diagnosis of Bearings using Ensemble and NaÏve Bayes Classifiers
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Condition-based maintenance involves maintaining equipment based on the real-time condition of its subsystems. Machine health monitoring typically involves analyzing signals such as vibration, temperature and acoustics, with vibration signature being the most commonly used parameter. Vibration analysis is considered to be a highly effective method for monitoring a machine's operating conditions. Its non-destructive nature makes it increasingly popular in industry, as it enables sustainable monitoring without disrupting the ongoing process. In some cases, the source of the vibration signal may be visible, allowing for corrective actions to be taken. However, in the majority of cases, components are hidden within the machine's structure, making it difficult to identify and locate the source of the signal. To address this challenge, sensors are strategically placed to detect signals produced by components that may need attention to prevent failures. In this article, non-contact fault diagnosis of bearings has been presented using Ensemble and Naïve Bayes classifiers. The findings indicate that the vibration signatures acquired from the developed non-contact sensor are consistent with the accelerometer under the same operational conditions.

articleTitle: Level Control of Coupled Tank System using Fuzzy PI Feedforward Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: This paper describes the Fuzzy based PI feedforward technique for controlling the liquid level of Tank 1 of the coupled tank system. The coupled tank system is a complex nonlinear system that requires precise control to accomplish the required liquid level of the tanks. A Fuzzy based PI feedforward controller is proposed to regulate the container's liquid level by changing the pump flow rates. The PI feedforward method is utilized to enhance the system's response. Fuzzy method is hybridizing to tune the proportional and integral gains. The simulation is done in MATLAB/Simulink environment. Finally, the simulated results are validated via Quanser® coupled tank experimental setup and show that the suggested control scheme is effective in improving the transient response of the coupled tank system in controlling the Tank 1 liquid level.

articleTitle: Adaptive Cruise Control Using Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: With the emergence of different machine learning and high-performance systems, the field of reinforcement learning has gained a plethora of interest from industry as well as researchers in the academic field. In this work, an algorithm known as twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient (TD3) that uses critic and actor networks is implemented to provide an efficient solution to the adaptive cruise control (ACC) problem. A reward function is used for the same that considers error in velocity and control input as parameters in addition to an extra term to give necessary push to reward function in case the error is less than a particular value. Two test cases are considered to substantiate the working effectiveness of the algorithm proposed. In one case normal driving scenario is considered while in the other test case a disturbance is modelled to replicate actual condition. From the results of the simulation and analysis, the operational efficacy of the put forward twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient algorithm is found out.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Object Detection Techniques for Automatic License Plate Recognition for Indian License Plates
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Automatic License Plate Recognition (ALPR) is a technology that allows for the automatic detection and recognition of license plates on vehicles. Deep learning models such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) have been applied to enhance license plate detection and character recognition capabilities, improving performance in situations involving distorted or skewed license plates. This paper compares the accuracy of various object detection techniques for License Plate Detection step in ALPR, and their results and performance are analyzed. These object detection techniques include traditional canny edge and contour segmentation, YOLOv5, Single Shot Detector (SSD), FasterRCNN, and RetinaNet. After comparison, it is found that YOLOv5 performs the best in accuracy and inference speed out of all the above-stated techniques.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Cell Balancing Techniques and Development of Active Cell Balancing Model Using Inductor
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: From last few years there is increase in the demand of electric vehicle, and battery is one of the important element of EV's [1]. As the Lithium-ion battery is one of the critical element and it can create cell imbalances inside the battery pack. The main reasons behind cell imbalances are aging effect, manufacturing defects, external atmospheric conditions. Due to these causes the internal resistance of lithium- ion cell will increase result in cell imbalances. These imbalances are in the range of 3-6%. There are basic two ways to balance all the cells in a Lithium-ion battery pack and that are Passive balancing and active balancing. In the passive balancing technique the extra energy from overcharge cell is dissipated in the form of heat through resistor in order to balance the cells where in active balancing energy transfer will take place from overcharge cell to undercharge cells through energy storing elements. This paper presents a cell balancing mechanism using a multiple inductor topology. The main advantage of this topology over capacitive balancing is high rate of balancing. Inductor based balancing is one of the simplest but effective way of balancing. This paper provides a practical approach of active balancing along with comparative analysis of different cell balancing topologies.

articleTitle: Virtual Community based Peer-to-Peer Energy Trading
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: With the increase in the use of renewable energy sources (RESs) and advances in technologies, peer-to-peer (P2P) energy trading is emerging as a promising approach to the local energy market. This work proposes a virtual community (VC) based P2P energy trading for buildings equipped with RES and flexible loads. A modified Nash bargaining solution is used for fair incentive distribution in the cooperative game. In this work, the equilibrium strategies of all players are obtained using a privacy-preserving decentralised approach. Shareable battery energy storage is considered in each VC, and Hong's 2m point estimation method is used to cope with the uncertainties associated with RESs.

articleTitle: Recent Advancements of Thermal Imaging in Induction Motor: A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: This paper offers an overview of thermal imaging measurements used for electrical equipment diagnosis. These machines, regardless of design, are all susceptible to failure when faults occur. Thermal Image Processing Technique can detect failure at an early stage and significantly lower maintenance costs. Infrared cameras capture thermal images of machines in their normal and fault conditions for further analysis. Modern infrared map techniques make infrared mapping techniques ideal for quickly and non-exhaustively measuring devices which would otherwise not be accessible. Thermal imaging relies on the detection and interpretation of infrared radiation that emanates from bodies when temperatures surpass absolute zero, creating visible pictures.

articleTitle: Smart Device for Electricity Management
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Electricity plays a vital role in our day to day activities. India happens to be the third biggest consumer of electricity in the whole world. Not only consumption, but electricity generation is also done in our country on a very large scale. The generated electricity is distributed using advanced technology even in rural areas now. The usage of electricity also has increased many folds during the recent years. Every house/ workplace has an electricity meter installed and a very vast network of government personnel work for monitoring the usage of electricity. The amount of electricity consumption in units is done not only in regular households but also academic institutes, corporate offices, farms, etc.. Electricity bill is received normally at the month end. Many times, due to certain glitches and irresponsible use of electricity, the bill amounts to a huge value. People know that majority of the electronic gadgets used day to day consume a lot of power; but still such devices are not immediately turned OFF after use. In addition some devices like irons, hair dryers, microwave ovens, etc get damaged too. Older appliances use more energy than newer ones. Till date, the traditional method of electricity billing is followed in almost all parts of India. The main drawback of this method is that no real time information is received by the consumers. It is the need of the hour to educate people about the importance of preservation of electricity so that the future generations are benefitted too. The patterns of electricity usage change in accordance with its daily usage. This change of consumption can be caused by a change in atmospheric conditions or irrelevant use of power like an increase of appliances in households. The factors may have a huge impact on the user. Most people neglect energy saving taking for granted the huge availability of the same. The main idea is to make people aware about their current electricity consumption levels. This paper proposes a smart device to monitor and control the use of electricity for efficient power consumption. The device designed uses ESP32 interfaced with peripherals including a Wi-Fi as well as Bluetooth module. The overall cost of the complete system is also affordable.

articleTitle: Internet of Things for Indian Electric Grid System: A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: With the ever-increasing population, the energy demand among consumers is also increasing rapidly and the present electric grid system is not able to cater to this demand. We need a modified and improved system which can cope with the demand for electric power. With the use of Internet of Things (IoT), in a grid communication system, a reliable and sustainable power network can be achieved. loT provides significant opportunities in the growth and development of electric power systems. Implementing Artificial intelligence in loT will enhance the performance of loT and eventually make a power system more reliable. However, there are many challenges to overcome in order to implement loT to achieve a complete energy efficient network. This paper highlights and promotes the role of loT in Power Systems. At the same time, it also analyzes the protocols and challenges faced in its implementation in India.

articleTitle: A Review on Recent Encoder-Decoder Architectures for Drivable Region Detection and Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: With the proliferation of science and technology, autonomous driving has garnered significant attention in the recent years due to the manifold benefits of driverless vehicles, including enhanced quality of life, mitigation of accidents, and curtailment of traffic congestion. In this work, recently developed encoder-decoder oriented architectures specifically designed to detect and segment the safe drivable region on roads have been reviewed, analyzed and compared, and the challenges in this field have been discussed. In pursuit of this objective, we initially furnish a survey of various orthodox and deep learning methods that find their use in detection of the road obstacles, and segmentation of roads and lane-lines. This is followed by a discussion on relevant field-oriented datasets. Subsequently, we present some recent encoder-decoder based methodologies such as HybridNets, You Only Look Once Panoptic (YOLOP), etc. These methods are then compared in terms of both inference speeds as well as performance metrics, to understand their potential in the real-time better, concluding that YOLOPv2 is currently the best suited architecture meant for drivable region detection. This is followed by an examination of challenges and unresolved inquiries in this domain.

articleTitle: Peer-to-Peer Energy Trading Using Blockchain in Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Over these years, there has been an observable effect on the environment due to Global Climatic Change. Scientists all over the world have predicted many of these disasters, and the main reason behind this is the emission of greenhouse gas. The use of fossil fuels to generate electricity contributes significantly to greenhouse gas emissions. If this conventional fossil fuel-based energy is replaced by renewable energy resources like solar energy, wind energy, etc., more than half of the emissions can be curbed. Increasing the usage of renewable sources of energy, mostly photovoltaic devices, and enabling distributed energy services will thereby encourage an energy trading environment among the users. This paper focuses on providing an approach to implement a prototype that integrates a microgrid and blockchain to trade electricity without an intermediary. It comprises of smart contracts and an interface which together forms a microgrid management system creating a peer-to-peer platform for users to trade electricity and thereby contributing towards sustainable and affordable energy.

articleTitle: Cyber Security in the Indian Electricity Distribution System: A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: Utilities are adopting automation in power systems to ensure reliability of power in Automated Active Distribution Network (AADN) and to meet the exponential increase in electricity demand. In this regard, communication infrastructures are increasingly embedded to facilitate real-time monitoring, supervisory and control of the systems requiring significant data exchange, thus, making distribution system vulnerable to cyber-attacks. In this regard, cyber security presents new challenges and there is a need to protect critical infrastructure in AADN. This paper aims to create an initial baseline of cyber security preparedness within the distribution electricity sector of India. The current states of cyber security in the Indian distribution system and the existing policies is investigated focusing challenges, gaps, and opportunities that may exist for future analysis.

articleTitle: Multi-Layer Model Classifier for Cyberattack Detection in Smart Electric Grid
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: In the Smart Grid, communication lines and physical open access points are always prone to cyber-attacks, and electric theft is the most common one. To detect electricity theft, researchers have developed several advanced machine learning models. However, existing work has not explored the problem of data imbalance properly, which is one of the significant challenges in electricity consumption data. This paper aims to compare various data balancing techniques and present an integrated theft detection model. This paper presents a multi-layer model for detecting fraudulent consumers in the smart grid. The detection process starts with data preparation steps, which include data interpolation, outlier handling, and data standardization. The next crucial step is handling data imbalance. Various techniques are tested, and AdaSys performs better than others. The model is being trained on a balanced dataset and validated on a real imbalanced dataset for realistic results. For higher performance, a two-layer model is chosen for electricity theft detection. The first layer consists of three heterogeneous machine learning models, and an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) model is used for the second layer. The first layer's probabilistic prediction serves as input to the second layer, which makes the final prediction. Experimental results confirm that multilayer model classifiers perform better than individual classifiers for detecting cyber-attacks on real consumption datasets.

articleTitle: Blockchain Based Banking Transactions Enabled by Big Data
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: The blockchain system has emerged as an innovative approach in a variety of areas, including. finance, supply chain, healthcare, education, and energy consumption. Although its extensive application, yet, there is a scarcity of in-depth studies to provide a thorough knowledge of blockchain technological advancement in various domains. As a result, the purpose of this comprehensive survey of literature is to examine the content analysis of 41 pertinent research articles and company surveys released from 2008 and 2023 were taken in order to evaluate the current state of blockchain technology's applications in the banking and financial services industry. The analysis examines the blockchain system's aspects, applications in financing, competitive edge, present state, and problems. Because of various limitations, the investigation suggests that the adoption of a blockchain-based financial management systems continues to be in its early stages. In summary, this study sheds light on the possible features of blockchain research in the financial sector and emphasizes the need for. further research to explore the potential of blockchain in the finance industry. The investigation is able to identify three key domains that need more investigation in order to establish blockchain systems as a disruptive system which will revolutionize the banking and finance industries. In conclusion, this investigation throws a spotlight on the prospective aspects of blockchain technology investigation in the banking and financial services industry.

publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment: Towards Flexible Green Energy Technologies (ICEPE)
abstract: It is our immense pleasure to welcome you to the 5th International Conference on Energy, Power, and Environment (ICEPE 2023), that is being organized by Department of Electrical Engineering, National Institute of Technology Meghalaya, on 15th to 17th June 2023.
